en: Śrī Harināma-cintāmaṇi;
Homage to Śrī Godruma-candra. Chapter One.
Victory to Gadādhara and Gaurāṅga, whose life is the Gaṅgā!
Victory to Sītā, Advaita, Śrīvāsa, and the multitude of devotees! (HNC 1.1)
On the shore of the salt ocean, on Mount Nīla, in the Śrī-mandira temple,
the wooden Brahman-puruṣa-pradhāna descended as an incarnation once the individual soul had been delivered.
It bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
In the age of Kali, Śrī Caitanya is the blessed Lord who has appeared in human form as a renunciant (sannyāsī) to make people understand the essential truth of the religious duties of this age.
Kāśī Miśra’s residence was the seat of authority. // HNC_1.3 //
May Kṛṣṇa become a wish-fulfilling tree for the multitude of His own devotees, bestowing love for Him upon all people;
and may I find happiness hearing the stories of the devotees from the mouths of devotees of various schools of thought.
One should give instruction on living beings with great care.
One day, after bathing in the ocean, the Lord met Śrī Siddhabakula Haridāsa with a joyful heart; desiring to know [the truth], he approached him with great care.
By what means can a living being cross over without effort? HNC_1.5 //
Placing his head at the Lord’s feet and offering many humble supplications, with tears flowing and his body covered in horripilation,
the noble Hari-dāsa remained there, longing and yearning again and again.
O Lord, Your divine play is profoundly deep.
We are utterly destitute; we have no wealth of learning, and your feet alone are our provisions.
Why do you ask such questions of us, unworthy persons, without cause?
What fruit will there be for the Lord Balarāma? // HNC_1.7 //
O Lord Kṛṣṇa, O All-pervading Master, You Yourself have descended as an incarnation in the abode of Navadvīpa to deliver the living beings; O Gaurarāya, show mercy and protect me with Your own limbs.
Then my heart was filled with joy. HNC_1.8 //
Your names are infinite, Your multitude of qualities is infinite,
and Your form is an ocean of bliss; Your pastimes are infinite, yet through Your grace, they have been made manifest.
O fool, taste this! HNC_1.9 //
O Sun composed of consciousness, I am but a particle of Your ray;
You are the Lord, and I am Your eternal servant.
O nectar of Your feet, grant me the great abundance of happiness; my hope is set upon the nectar of Your name. HNC_1.10 //
O Master, though I am a lowly mother and know how to speak,
I shall nevertheless carry out Your command;
by Your power, I shall speak from my mouth for Your pleasure.
One should not take account of faults or virtues.
Kṛṣṇa is the sole reality, consisting solely of will; Kṛṣṇa is the Lord of all.
Through His eternal possession of power, Kṛṣṇa is the all-pervading one, higher than the highest. (HNC 1.12)
O Kṛṣṇa! O Kṛṣṇa’s power! O Kṛṣṇa’s power! There is nothing independent of Kṛṣṇa; that which is power is called Kṛṣṇa—so says the Vedic mantra. (HNC 1.13)
O all-pervading Kṛṣṇa, whose very nature is power and majesty; O Kṛṣṇa, within infinite majesty, You alone are the one form.
The threefold power of manifestation is that very manifestation itself; the all-pervading one is merely the experience of manifestation. // HNC 1.15 //
O fair-limbed, beautiful one, Your glory is threefold: consciousness, the insentient, and the individual soul; these are the objects of the scriptures. (HNC 1.16)
The infinite splendor of consciousness, Vaikuṇṭha, and so forth, from which the abode of Kṛṣṇa arises;
Govinda, Śrī-Kṛṣṇa, Hari, and so forth, from which the names arise. HNC 1.17.
His form is manifold, beginning with the two-armed holder of the flute;
His nature is manifold, beginning with the quality of bestowing bliss upon devotees. HNC 1.18.
The *rasa*-līlā of Vraja in Navadvīpa is the congregational chanting (*saṅkīrtana*); such are the wonderful enumerations of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes. (HNC 1.19)
This entire splendor of consciousness is non-material; it appears as the phenomenal world through the perspective of worldly manifestation. (HNC 1.20)
The essence of the reality of Viṣṇu is the collection of the activities of consciousness; sing repeatedly in the Veda the offering to the station of Viṣṇu. HNC 1.21.

The reality of Viṣṇu, which is the spiritual sovereignty of Kṛṣṇa, is the pure reality; it possesses no material qualities nor is it a transformation of māyā. The reality of Viṣṇu transcends the insentient and is the essence of pure existence (sattva). (HNC 1.22)
Pure sattva is devoid of the scent of rajas and tamas;
that which is mixed with rajas and tamas is well known as mixed sattva. HNC 1.23.
Govinda, Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, who lies within the causal waters,
who lies within the Garbhodaka ocean, and who lies upon the shore of the milk-ocean.
O Lord, come; You are the portion of Your own self, the familiar incarnation, who is the essence of the principle of Viṣṇu and pure goodness in its entirety.
Whether in Goloka, Vaikuṇṭha, or even in the causal ocean, or else remaining in this very inert world,
he bears the name of Viṣṇu. (HNC 1.26)
This very inert universe entered [Him], the sovereign of Māyā;
the all-pervading Lord of all gods obtained the name Viṣṇu. (HNC 1.27)
The Lord of Māyā is the possessor of Māyā, composed of pure sattva;
those of mixed sattva include Brahmā, Śiva, and all others. (HNC 1.28)
The entire reality of Viṣṇu and the abode of Viṣṇu are the expansion of Your conscious majesty;
O Lord, they are Your conscious majesty and the theater of Your divine play.
The manifestation of the acid-tattva consists of the principle of māyā and all things beyond this;
the manifestation of the acit-tattva consists of the fourteen worlds. (HNC 1.30)
O powerful one, the majesty of Māyā is the abode of the Goddess;
it consists of the five elements, mind, intellect, and ego. HNC 1.31.
These are the Bhūrloka, Bhuvarloka, and Svargaloka; the Maharloka, Janaloka, Tapoloka, Satyaloka, and Brahmaloka. // HNC_1.32 //
O Lord of the World, may the seven lower worlds, beginning with Atala and Sutala, be filled with Your illusory splendor! HNC_1.33 //
The full reality of the glory of consciousness is the savior from the shadow of *māyā*;
the glory of the individual soul (*jīva*) is the nature of the atom of consciousness, which is the mode of the soul's glory. HNC 1.34.
O Jīva, by virtue of the nature of consciousness, you are independent in your movement; having calculated [the means], your purpose is infinite bliss and liberation. HNC 1.35.
For the sake of that very bliss, the liberated souls chose Kṛṣṇa;
they remain as the attendants of Kṛṣṇa in their liberated forms. (HNC 1.36)
Or, when the bound soul, whose face is turned outward, again forms the mental conception of its own happiness,
it directs its desire toward Māyā who stands by its side. (HNC 1.37)
All of them became eternally turned away from Kṛṣṇa;
in the realm of the Goddess, they obtained bodies created by Māyā. (HNC 1.38)
Now, the wheel of meritorious and sinful karma has fallen;
it constantly revolves within the body, which is its gross form. (HNC 1.39)
Sometimes rising to heaven, sometimes falling into hell,
he wandered and wandered through the eighty-four thousand species of existence.
Nevertheless, O Lord Kṛṣṇa, You are compassionate; Your majesty is such that even a living soul may become Yours.
It is certain that You always contemplate the welfare of Your servant.
O Servant, please bestow with compassion that which you seek out as happiness. (HNC 1.42)
Through Your grace, those who seek impermanent happiness within the power of Māyā— the realm of worldly auspicious karma and ritual action— shall attain it without effort. HNC 1.43.
Since virtuous action is the means for attaining happiness, it consists of the stainless sacrifice of Dharma, yoga, fire-offerings, and vows. HNC 1.44.
May all your virtuous deeds always be composed of insentient matter; may the activity of consciousness never meet with them. HNC 1.45.
The means for attaining those [pleasures] results in a fruit consisting of insentient matter;
the enjoyment and happiness of the higher worlds are more powerful than that. (HNC 1.46)
All experiences of karmic fruition are not the peace of the self;
therefore, to exert effort toward them is a profound delusion. (HNC 1.47)
Having employed all auspicious karmas as means, he accomplished the impermanent goals and bestowed happiness upon the world. // HNC_1.48 //
If ever a saint, through association with the virtuous, knows the means of deliverance from these six states, may he be able to save me,
this soul, the servant of Kṛṣṇa.
By means of which illusion [one goes] to the further shore. // HNC_1.49 //
That which is produced merely by the fruit of rare virtuous deeds—the trivial ritual section (karmakāṇḍa)—is not what has been ordained. HNC 1.50.
Know that the section on knowledge (jñāna-kāṇḍa), as well as the bliss of absorption into Brahman, is merely the bondage of māyā.
One who strives for the attainment of liberation is indeed a wise man. HNC 1.51.
O Compassionate One, you are the source of all the worlds;
you have certainly bestowed the section on knowledge, the science of Brahman. (HNC 1.52)
Relying on the doctrine of Māyā, you claim that the inert becomes liberated and that the individual soul (jīva) merges into Brahman. HNC 1.53.
What is the reality of Brahman? That very Brahman is the light of the splendor of Your limbs; because it is situated beyond the dustless state, it is absorption (laya). HNC 1.54.
Viṣṇu brings about the destruction of all those asuras; he himself is that Brahmā who has crossed beyond Māyā. (HNC 1.55)
Both the performer of external rituals for Kṛṣṇa and the scholar are turned away from Kṛṣṇa; neither ever tastes the bliss of service to Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 1.56)
Virtuous action is directed toward devotion; that virtuous action is preeminent which is itself directed toward devotion.
The fruit of that is for the living being to drink from the company of devotees and holy men.
O horse, one who possesses faith should associate with the devotees of Kṛṣṇa;
he should have a taste for the Name, compassion for living beings, and maintain the path of devotion. HNC 1.58.
O Ocean of Mercy, Lord of living beings, You show compassion toward both the practitioner of action and the man of knowledge by providing the secondary path;
You are intent upon uplifting those practitioners of action and men of knowledge who are turned away from the Divine.
For those people who are travelers on the path of action and the path of knowledge, your exertion is for their upliftment. HNC 1.60.
O Mother, thinking of the welfare of every traveler, you have kept the path of secondary devotion as the sole way. (HNC 1.61)
In the *karmīra* category, the *karmera* follows the path of secondary devotion (*gauṇa-bhakti*);
remaining within the system of social classes and stages of life (*varṇāśrama*), he practices devotion amidst his ritual duties while maintaining the path of the secondary devotee. (HNC 1.62)
O Tārā, having purified the heart of all performed actions,
you have caused [the veil] to disappear and established them within the seed of faith.
The wise one has placed me on the secondary path; by the power of his virtuous deeds and grace toward devotion,
he has established me as a seed of faith within the state of exclusive devotion.
O Lord, by the ripening of my past deeds, you have become my servant;
I desire nothing other than to abandon me for some trivial fruit. HNC 1.65.
Know this: for them there is supreme auspiciousness;
having cast aside both worldly enjoyment and liberation, He grants the fruit of devotion.
For one who proceeds according to their own inclination through the process of the secondary path,
faith is granted in that secondary path, the path of devotion (bhakti-mārga). // HNC_1.67 //
O Lord, You are full of compassion; by Your grace alone, O Compassionate One, can any living being become pure? For without Your grace, who could ever be purified? 1.68
In the Kali age, the path of the secondary [devotion] has fallen into a state of wretchedness;
in the Satya Yuga, it was practiced by hosts of sages through the yoga of meditation.
Now, O Lord, having purified it, You have bestowed Your own treasure of devotion.
In the Tretā Yuga, the sacrificial rites were purified in many ways;
in the Dvāpara [Yuga], the path of worship was filled with devotion. (HNC 1.70)
O Lord, seeing the miserable state of living beings at the arrival of the Kali age, You completely abandoned both knowledge and the path of action.
Short life, much suffering,
and the decline of strength and intellect— all these calamities have been made into food for living beings. (HNC 1.72)
The path of the duties of the social orders and stages of life, as well as Sāṅkhya and Yoga knowledge,
will not be effective once the living beings of the Kali age have been uplifted.
Devotion that has entered the path of knowledge and ritual action is a secondary path; it has become a wrong path, crowded with thorns. (HNC 1.74)
When one holds fast to separate means for the sake of attaining the goal, obstacles become manifold in the life of a living being. (HNC 1.75)
O Lord, you are the primary path for the contemplation of the Name; having taken concern for the welfare of living beings,
you yourself have descended in the Kali age along with the Name.
In this age where the laws of the yugas prevail, the chanting of the holy name is the primary path by which living beings obtain the wealth of love for Kṛṣṇa.
In the remembrance of Nāma and the chanting of Nāma—this alone is the dharma that a living being must practice. (HNC 1.78)

In the process of the non-duality between the means (*upāya*) and the goal (*upeya*), as well as between the object to be accomplished (*sādhya*) and the instrument of accomplishment (*sādhana*), whatever is primarily the name becomes the very thing to be accomplished; thus, no distinction remains between the means and the goal. (HNC 1.79)
There is no obstacle in the accomplishment of what is to be achieved;
by Your grace, O Jīva, one crosses over without effort. HNC 1.80.
O most base one, you do not even worship my name; O exceedingly deluded one, you have failed in your duty toward me.
O Brahma-Haridāsa, look at this stream of tears;
he has dropped his sighs at the feet of the Lord.
For one whose only nourishment is the delight in devotion to the Lord Hari, the *Harināmacintāmaṇi* is their very life. (HNC 1.83)
Thus ends the first chapter, titled "The Indication of the Majesty of the Name," in the *Śrī-Hari-Nāma-Cintāmaṇi*.
(2) The second chapter: "An Investigation into the Taking of the Name."
Victory to Gaurāṅga, whose life is the Gaṅgā! Victory to Sītā, who is non-dual with Him! Victory to Śrīvāsa and the assembly of devotees! HNC_2.1 //
Due to great love, Haridāsa wept; out of love, Gauracandra gave him an embrace. (HNC 2.2)
With strength equal to a thunderbolt, you are the abode of devotion;
you are the knower of all principles and forever beyond illusion. HNC_2.3 //
The excellence of exclusive devotion is demonstrated by [the Lord] appearing even in a lowly family;
for Kṛṣṇa is not found through wealth, honor, noble lineage, or virtuous character. (HNC 2.4)
He who possesses supreme faith in the worship of no other, and who has regard for the deity as the highest—that person is a great soul. (HNC 2.5)
The reality of the Name, the essence of all things, known as the mastership of the servant of Śrī Hari, is understood by you;
you are a master in conduct and a scholar in its propagation. (HNC 2.6)
O Balarāma, the glory of the Name is boundless;
having heard it from your mouth, joy has arisen within me. (HNC 2.7)
One who has the name of a Vaiṣṇava on his lips is indeed a Vaiṣṇava; one should certainly honor such a person with effort, even if he is a householder. (HNC 2.8)
One who constantly hears the name of Kṛṣṇa from the mouth of an excellent Vaiṣṇava is indeed that most excellent Vaiṣṇava,
the abode of all virtues.
The characteristic of the most excellent Vaiṣṇava is this:
upon seeing such a supreme Vaiṣṇava, the name of Kṛṣṇa resides in his mouth and devotion to Kṛṣṇa is found within him. (HNC 2.10)
O Jīva, in what form shall I perform this worship of Kṛṣṇa’s name? Please tell me the procedure for that. (HNC 2.11)
With his voice faltering with love and eyes filled with tears, Haridāsa spoke these words with great strength. // HNC_2.12 //
The essential nature of the name is the name of Kṛṣṇa—the wish-fulfilling gem, beginningless, and composed of consciousness.
That which is Kṛṣṇa is that very name; they are one single reality. (HNC 2.13)
The reality named Caitanyavigraha is eternally liberated; the distinction between name and the named is a conventional standpoint, for he is eternally pure being. (HNC 2.14)
In this inert world, Your imperishable form exists as the essence of aesthetic flavor; O Connoisseur of Rasa, You have descended as an incarnation of pure being.
The object of knowledge is Kṛṣṇa, who is understood through four attributes:
name, form, quality, and action, which have been established from beginningless time.
That which is eternally established,
the eternal reality, non-different from Kṛṣṇa whose nature is rasa— through acquaintance with these four, it becomes an established reality. (HNC 2.17)
Through the power of the *sandhinī*, there is familiarity with its movement;
it is renowned as eternally perfected in form, always consisting of consciousness. (HNC 2.18)
O Kṛṣṇa, attract all people throughout the entire universe;
they are eternally devoted to Dharma, and their only wealth is the name of Kṛṣṇa.
The form of Kṛṣṇa is eternal;
the form of Kṛṣṇa is eternally non-different from Kṛṣṇa himself. Name and form are one and the same reality; there is no distinction between them. (HNC 2.20)
When one remembers the name Śrī, such forms appear in succession;
the names and forms, though distinct, dance in various colors according to different modes. (HNC 2.21)
The qualities of Kṛṣṇa are eternal; His sixty-four qualities are infinite and boundless, and all the incarnations are His own partial manifestations. HNC 2.22.
In the portion of his qualities, he is Brahmā, Śiva, and other lords;
in his qualities, he is Nārāyaṇa, the lord of sixty qualities. (HNC 2.23)
All these are eternal qualities; His names are eternal, infinite in number, and pervade Vaikuṇṭha and His activities.
The eternality of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes is the quality by which His pastimes expand; Goloka, Vaikuṇṭha, and Vraja are all of the nature of consciousness. (HNC 2.25)
Name, form, and quality belong to the reality of consciousness.
Līlā is distinct from the object; it arises as non-different from name, form, quality, and activity.
In the case of the bound soul (jīva) in contact with the insentient (acit), it appears as different. // HNC_2.26 //
In the pure soul, name, form, quality, and action are one; this difference residing in the inert body is what is called discrimination. (HNC 2.27)
O Kṛṣṇa, there is no trace of insentient matter; therefore, meditate upon Him whose nature consists solely of name, form, qualities, and pastimes. (HNC 2.28)
Regarding the fact that name is the root of all things, among these four types of acquaintance, name is the first of them all; it is recognized as being of every form. (HNC 2.29)
Therefore, the dharma of a Vaiṣṇava consists of the Name alone;
within the Name, His form, qualities, and activities are fully manifest. (HNC 2.30)
The entirety of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes exists within His name;
that name is the supreme reality, Your own ordinance.
Whether it be a Vaiṣṇava or one who is predominantly Vaiṣṇava, that distinction exists through the assistance of the faith of the soul bound by name;
the Vaiṣṇava takes him up in his pure form and delivers him. (HNC 2.32)
One whose manifestation is primarily that of the Name becomes like a Vaiṣṇava;
by the power of Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, he gradually attains pure devotion. (HNC 2.33)
In this illusory world, the name of Kṛṣṇa and the living being—these two alone are the activity of consciousness; there is no other substance equal to them in this cycle of existence.
In that treasury of Kṛṣṇa, the name is the supreme wealth. (HNC 2.34)
The individual soul has taken up the name of Kṛṣṇa within its own conscious activity;
it has taken up the entire worldly realm of saṃsāra. (HNC 2.35)

There are two types of names, distinguished as primary (*mukhya*) and secondary (*gauṇa*); the name of Kṛṣṇa is likewise of two kinds. By taking refuge in the primary name, the living being attains the essence of all things. (HNC 2.36)
Taking as its basis each of His various pastimes, every name of Kṛṣṇa is a primary name, the abode of all qualities. (HNC 2.37)
His primary names are Govinda, Gopāla, Rāma, Śrī-Nandanandana,
Rādhānātha, Hari, and Yaśomatīprāṇadhana.
O Madanamohana, Śyāmasundara, Mādhava, Lord of the Gopīs, Protector of Vraja, and Yādava! HNC_2.39 //
This form is the eternal revealer of pastimes, and its name; by chanting all of these, the living being attains the abode of Kṛṣṇa.
The secondary name and its definition are for the purpose of identifying primordial nature (prakṛti);
it is accepted by the Vedas that the secondary [name] resides in the qualities (guṇa) of primordial nature. (HNC 2.41)
The Supreme Self is the creator of the universe, Brahmā is the sustainer, and Hara, the Lord of Sacrifice, is the destroyer and protector of the world. HNC_2.42 //
In this manner, the difference between the fruits of primary and secondary names— pertaining respectively to the sections on ritual action (karma-kāṇḍa) and knowledge (jñāna-kāṇḍa)—
is that they bestow merit and liberation, as agreed upon by the scriptures. (HNC 2.43)
The primary fruit of chanting the name is the wealth of love for Kṛṣṇa;
the assembly of saints attains that primarily through the name alone.
O friend, there is no difference in the result whether the name of Kṛṣṇa alone enters the mouth externally,
or whether it goes into the path of hearing within. (HNC 2.45)
Whether one is of pure caste or of impure caste, the living being crosses over by means of this scripture; such is the conclusion of this treatise. (HNC 2.46)
However, there is one story here that is certain: if the name alone remains, there will be delay in attaining welfare. (HNC 2.47)
Even if there is only the appearance of the Name, it is another form of auspiciousness; the wealth of love will arise solely through delay. (HNC 2.48)
When the semblance of name has been destroyed through the exhaustion of sin, the pure Name arises; at that very moment, one certainly attains love for Śrī Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 2.49)
Whether there is a separation or a fault in the separation, there may indeed be an offense; however, by that very offense, there arises an obstacle to the attainment of love. (HNC 2.50)
The conceptual distinction between the name and the named constitutes an intervention; as long as this intervention remains, love can never be attained. (HNC 2.51)
There are two kinds of intervention:
intervention by phoneme and intervention by meaning;
the Veda prescribes these two types of intervention. (HNC 2.52)
The doctrine called Māyāvāda creates an obscuration of reality; this Māyāvāda is a wicked philosophy.
It is a web of deception in the Kali age, and is not approved by this scripture. (HNC 2.53)
The name that is not pierced by any obstruction is called the pure name;
therefore, one who has the pure name of Kṛṣṇa upon their lips should always be known as a Vaiṣṇava and served with joy. (HNC 2.54)
Since that which is useless has perished, the state of being a pseudo-name (nāmābhāsa) is likewise removed; one attains the manifestation of the name consisting of pure consciousness.
To pierce through the pseudo-name and obtain the pure name, the living being must serve a true guru with effort and cooperation. (HNC 2.55)
At the very moment one partakes of that which destroys all misfortune,
the tongue of devotion dances with the name of the nature of consciousness.
The stream of nectar called his name does not cease;
intoxicated by its flavor, the living being dances uncontrollably. (HNC 2.57)
When the Name dances, the living soul dances; when the Name dances, the wealth of love dances; when the world dances, Māyā flees away. (HNC 2.58)
That which is called faith is indeed called authority; within it lies all power.
Authority has been bestowed by the Name upon every human being, while all power has been ordained by the Lord through the Name. (HNC 2.59)
He who has faith in the Name is the qualified one;
he in whose mouth the name of Kṛṣṇa resides is the true practitioner. (HNC 2.60)
There is no restriction regarding place, time, impurity, and so forth; indeed, at all times, the taking of the holy Name is more powerful than those [restrictions]. (HNC 2.61)

In the Kali age, only by having sincere faith in the Name does one gain the right to it; as for giving, sacrifice, ritual bathing, and chanting, there is no such consideration—merely through faith in the congregational chanting of Kṛṣṇa’s names, one gains the right. (HNC 2.62)
In this age of strife, those who take refuge with single-minded faith in the name of Hari achieve all attainments.
O living beings, in this Kali age which is devoid of guile, remain established in the world of Kṛṣṇa and always chant the name of Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 2.64)
One should grasp objects favorable to devotion, avoid objects unfavorable to it,
perform all actions conducive to devotion,
and abandon everything that is contrary to devotion. (HNC 2.65)
Remaining in the world of transmigration, Kṛṣṇa spent his life constantly remembering the name of Hari. // HNC_2.66 //
One should utter the name [of the Lord] with undivided consciousness and never perform any other religious rite;
one should worship no other than the independent Lord of Knowledge. (HNC 2.67)
One should constantly perform service to the devotees of Kṛṣṇa’s name;
then the attainment of love for Kṛṣṇa will surely come to them. (HNC 2.68)
Haridāsa fell at the feet of the Lord Kāṅdi;
placing his hands upon those feet, he prayed for devotion to His name.
Haridāsa took his place at the feet of Bhaktivinoda;
for him, the *Harināma Cintāmaṇi* was his very life. (HNC 2.70)
Thus ends the first chapter, titled "An Investigation into the Taking of the Name," in the *Śrī-Hari-nāma-cintāmaṇi*.
(3) Third Chapter.
Victory to Gaurāṅga, whose life is the Gaṅgā, who has shattered the mace of conceptualizing the appearance of names!
Victory to Sītā, the non-dual, and to the devotees such as Śrīvāsa and others! HNC_3.1 //
Mahāprabhu, having become compassionate toward Haridāsa,
rose up at that moment and extended his lotus-like hand.
O Śuna Haridāsa, listen to my words;
understand now clearly the nature of the semblance of the Name. HNC 3.3.
When the appearance of name is understood, the name becomes pure;
effortlessly, the living being will cross over by means of the qualities of the name. (HNC 3.4)
The cloud of the appearance of names, which is the form of ignorance and misfortune, is like the sun; it destroys the darkness of *māyā*.
Yet, that which is called "cloud" and "mist" repeatedly obscures [the light]. (HNC 3.5)
All the ignorance and misfortunes of the living being become powerful, appearing like a thick bank of dark clouds. (HNC 3.6)
The sun of Kṛṣṇa’s name has risen in the sky of the mind; once again, the clouds of delusion have covered it. (HNC 3.7)
Ignorance, anger, delusion regarding one's true nature, and the failure to know that which is the very nature of consciousness—
this ignorance brings about the darkness of the internal fog. (HNC 3.8)
O Kṛṣṇa, Lord of All! He who does not know Bali wanders on the path of ritual action, worshipping various deities. (HNC 3.9)
For one who has no knowledge of the true nature of the living soul, there is constant ignorance regarding Māyā, which is the locus of the insentient. HNC 3.10.
Then Haridāsa said, "Today I am blessed;
I shall hear the Name and the stories of Caitanya from your own mouth. (HNC 3.11)
O Kṛṣṇa, O Jīva, O Servant of the Lord! Māyā is insentient by nature; upon the heads of those who do not know her lies the shadow of ignorance. (HNC 3.12)
Clouds, harmful non-existent craving, weakness of heart, offenses, non-existent craving, and weakness of heart, offenses.
All these misfortunes are obstructed by the form of the cloud. // HNC_3.13 //
Just as the light of the sun's rays is eclipsed by a name, always shroud the self-established name of Kṛṣṇa with a name. (HNC 3.14)
As long as there is no knowledge of the reality of the relationship with the limit (avadhi),
that manifestation of name remains the locus of the individual soul. (HNC 3.15)
O practitioner, although you have taken refuge in a true guru, if you lack skill in devotion, obstacles such as clouds and the like will remain far away. HNC 3.16.
The connection, the subject matter, and the purpose—
may the sun named Megha Kujjhaṭika dispel these clouds and,
becoming radiant, bestow the boon of love upon His devotees. (HNC 3.17)
Having gained knowledge through the connection with a true guru, one should offer it;
one should practice the study of the Name by means of its expressed meaning. HNC 3.18.
The sun named "Name" (nāma-sūrya), having become powerful in a very short time, strikes down the thick fog of misfortune. (HNC 3.19)
The reality of the purpose is the wealth of love;
a living being who has attained that love performs the congregational chanting of the Name. (HNC 3.20)
The knowledge of the relationship [between the self and the Divine] arises at the feet of the true guru, with the assistance of faith in the living being;
first, the knowledge of the relationship is attained through profound reflection. (HNC 3.21)
Kṛṣṇa is eternally the Lord and the soul is eternally His servant;
love for Kṛṣṇa is the eternal manifestation of the soul's true nature.
The living being, who is the eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa, has forgotten that;
wandering in the illusory world, he seeks happiness. (HNC 3.23)
The illusory world is the prison of the living being; it is a punitive retribution for the fault of the soul’s aversion [to the Supreme]. (HNC 3.24)
Then, if a living being is a virtuous Vaiṣṇava by the grace [of the Lord], he attains knowledge of the relationship [to Kṛṣṇa] and again receives the name of Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 3.25)
Then one attains the wealth of love, the essence of all dharma; compared to this, the states of sāyujya and the like are contemptible. (HNC 3.26)
As long as the knowledge of the relationship [between word and object] is not stable, so long will names appear as a basis for what is meaningless. (HNC 3.27)
The fruit of chanting the Name is the manifestation of the Name; at that time, many auspicious signs appear.
For the living being, powerful past virtuous deeds (sukṛti) will inevitably manifest. (HNC 3.28)
When the semblance of the Name is lost, sin remains; when there is liberation through the semblance of the Name, Kali is destroyed. (HNC 3.29)
In the manifestation of the Name, there is the purification of the noble lineages of men and horses;
in the manifestation of the Name, there is the warding off of all diseases. (HNC 3.30)
All doubt regarding the appearance of names is dispelled at a distance;
the appearance of names brings peace from all misfortunes. (HNC 3.31)
O assembly of yakṣas, rāk�sāsas, bhūtas, pretas, and grahas: at the mere mention of this name, may all misfortunes go far away. HNC_3.32 //
When people fallen into hell attain happiness and liberation, all their *prārabdha* karma vanishes like a mere name. (HNC 3.33)
Superior to all the Vedas and greater than all sacred fords, the mere mention of the Name is more excellent than all auspicious deeds. (HNC 3.34)
The manifestation of the Name bestows Vaikuṇṭha and other realms;
it is the giver of the fourfold aims of life—dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa.
In this manifestation of the Name, which possesses all powers, the Name is the protector of living beings.
O bringer of joy to the world, bestower of the supreme state; O sole refuge for the helpless, the most excellent station for all. HNC 3.36.
The attainment of worlds such as Vaikuṇṭha is merely a semblance of a name;
this is especially so according to all the scriptures in the Kali age.
Convention, jest, praise, and play— know that these four types are merely semblances of names.
One should consider it as a conventional sign, a jest, a ritual exclamation (stobha), or a playful gesture.
Regarding the two modes of manifestation as the form of convention and as the name, one should dissolve the name into Viṣṇu by taking him as the object of focus through dull intellect;
otherwise, one should utter the name while taking Viṣṇu as the object of focus. (HNC 3.39)
In this convention, there are two kinds of what appear to be names;
Ajāmila is the witness to this, as it is revealed in the scriptures. (HNC 3.40)
The Yavanas shall all be liberated without effort;
they shall cry out "Hārāma! Hārāma! at the mere sound of the Name. HNC_3.41 //
Even if, apart from conventional designation, there were no appearance of a name,
nevertheless, there would be neither the power of the name nor the destruction of the horse.
Whoever utters the name of Kṛṣṇa even in jest or as a mere semblance of a name in play,
that person crosses over this worldly existence, becoming equal to Jarāsandha.
The appearance of names,
the gestures of the limbs, and the name-appearance equal to that of Caidya—
when these consist of mere *stobha*, the bonds of worldly existence are destroyed. (HNC 3.44)
Out of playfulness, they did not give their names, nor did they feel any contempt;
because of the power of Kṛṣṇa and Rāma, their names appeared as mere play. (HNC 3.45)
All these people who merely imitate names cross over as members of the barbarian hordes; those sensualists and lazy folk follow this path.
Faith, sport, and the manifestation of names are distinct; through faith one performs that which is accompanied by the purpose of the name.
Faith is indeed that which has been ordained for you. (HNC 3.47)
One who holds a contemptuous attitude toward everything from conventional symbols up to the ultimate nature, and who treats the Name with indifference, having abandoned faith— HNC 3.48.
Even from the mere appearance of the Name, it is called "playful sport";
by that alone one attains liberation and sin is destroyed. (HNC 3.49)
When the destruction of misfortune occurs, the semblance of the Name (nāmābhāsa) bestows love;
yet, having abandoned love for Kṛṣṇa, one attains everything through the semblance of the Name. Furthermore, through the semblance of the Name, the pure Name itself comes to be attained.
When one is free from all that is harmful, the name becomes pure;
then, it is certain that Kṛṣṇa-love will arise within them. (HNC 3.51)
When the manifestation of the Name bestows love directly upon the person, one should offer that love to the Name according to the prescribed injunctions. HNC 3.52.
The semblance of the Name is a variety of the offense against the Name; therefore, one should avoid the offense against the Name.
One should bow down to those who produce the semblance of the Name. (HNC 3.53)
Knowledge is infinitely superior to action;
know that the one called Bali is the Lord of All in essence. (HNC 3.54)
If faith rooted in delight arises within a state of purity, then the emergence of what is called "complete purification" will occur. (HNC 3.55)
Reflection and image are two types of appearance; reflection is called "name-appearance," while image is "appearance-appearance.
Thus, there are two kinds of appearance. Reflection is [the first].
The two types of semblances of faith are all your illusion.
In the appearance of faith, there is the appearance of the name "Shadow";
through that appearance of the name, the auspicious [state] of the living being arises. (HNC 3.57)

One who brings the reflection of one's own mind— the appearance of faith— into their heart, having cultivated pure faith toward another living being known as a "reflection" (pratibimba), attains the vision [of the Self]. (HNC 3.58)
At that time, the desire for enjoyment or liberation remains constant day and night; one strives both by day and by night to obtain the desired goal without exertion. (HNC 3.59)
Faith that consists merely of the characteristic of faith—bring that here;
its reflection is called "semblance-faith" in the treatise. (HNC 3.60)
Because there is the appearance of faith and the appearance of names within the reflection, the appearances of reflection and name continue without ceasing. (HNC 3.61)

In this appearance of names called "reflections," the deceit of Māyāvāda arises; through this appearance of names, the wicked doctrine of Māyāvāda is produced and, by means of craftiness, it becomes fully developed. (HNC 3.62)
Forming the notion that the Name is a mere deceptive reflection, a semblance, a fault, or something to be constantly achieved through effort,
one destroys the majesty of the Name and dies within one's own transgression.
There is a distinction between the appearance called a shadow and the appearance called a reflection:
in the case of the appearance called a shadow, there is merely ignorance;
due to weakness of heart, it brings about misfortune. (HNC 3.64)
All faults are cleansed by means of the Name;
in the appearance of the Name as a reflection, there is an increase of faults. (HNC 3.65)
Māyāvāda and bhakti— these two are mutually contradictory doctrines;
Māyāvāda is an offense against everything pertaining to Kṛṣṇa’s name, form, qualities, and pastimes.
In the view of the proponents of illusion (māyāvādins), everything is false and perishable.
The essence of love is not eternal;
it is certain that Māyāvāda is contrary to devotion.
The Māyāvāda is counted among the enemies of devotion;
therefore, O slayer of offenses, destroy the Māyāvādin! HNC 3.68.
In the mouth of a proponent of illusion (māyāvādin), there is no name that is external;
yet even for a name that is external, the state of being a name is not lost.
If a proponent of illusion (māyāvādī) utters the name, he will suffer a fall by receiving an offering of power upon that which is impermanent.
In the presence of Nāma, there is the prayer for both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
in the presence of Nāma, deceit results in torment.

When will the offender who professes Māyāvāda ever abandon it? If he abandons the hope for worldly enjoyment and liberation, and performs the chanting of the Name, he becomes a servant of Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 3.72)
Then he abandons the wicked doctrine of Māyāvāda;
accompanied by repentance, he becomes a follower of the Name. (HNC 3.73)
Furthermore, by performing hearing and chanting in the association of the saintly,
at that very moment, the knowledge of the true relationship arises, which delivers one from the ocean of worldly existence.
If tears fall from the eyes at the mere mention of his name, and the mind becomes strong upon receiving even a trace of his compassion; HNC_3.75 //

In devotion, the impermanent is powerful; this is the offense of Māyāvāda. The form of Kṛṣṇa and service to Kṛṣṇa are the very nature of the living entity. All things imagined by the impermanent Māyāvāda are powerless. (HNC 3.76)
By this offense, one is counted among the proponents of illusion;
the doctrine of illusion is the mine of all sophists. (HNC 3.77)

To the person who professes Māyāvāda, this semblance of a name—which is itself a semblance of reasoning—bestows the attainment of union (*sāyujya*). This wish-fulfilling tree of a name-bestowal grants his desired goal: the *nirvāṇa* of union. (HNC 3.78)
Although it possesses all powers, it appears as if devoid of name; though it is a reflection, it gives the appearance of liberation. (HNC 3.79)
Among the five kinds of liberation, Sāyujya is merely an appearance;
when the fruits consist solely in the destruction of worldly existence and afflictions, there is the destruction of everything. HNC 3.80.
The proponent of illusion does not obtain eternal bliss; rather, people deluded by illusion consider that [state] to be happiness.
In the liberation of union (*sāyujya-nirvāṇa*), they obtain merely the semblance of happiness. // HNC_3.81 //
Service to the Absolute Reality, Consciousness, and Bliss is the supreme liberation;
there is no attainment of union with Him for one whose remembrance of Kṛṣṇa has ever been destroyed. (HNC 3.82)
If there is no devotion, love, constancy, or faith, how can the light of eternal bliss be revealed to him? (HNC 3.83)

O one of evil mind, if you do not enter into the semblance of the shadow-name, you will eventually obtain the pure name; yet, O evil-minded one, you do not recognize that it is no longer the semblance of the shadow-name. If the power of the mind is not present in the doctrine of the [true] mind, he is destroyed. (HNC 3.84)
He who does not know the true power—that power is the very nature of what is called the gift of knowledge. HNC 3.85.
When the sun is obscured by clouds, its radiance is not perceived;
however, when the cloud has vanished, the sun causes it to arise. // HNC_3.86 //
O Dhanya, by the power of the true guru, one who bears his name as a mere shadow attains love for the Name effortlessly in a few days. HNC 3.87.
One must certainly abandon the company of those who propound Māyā;
having abandoned the company of Māyāvādīs along with their sophistry, one shall find satisfaction by serving those who are devoted solely to the pure Name. (HNC 3.88)
O Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, that soul alone is blessed who obeys Your command. (HNC 3.89)
O Nāpāla, those who do not follow your command are like living ashes; even in ten million lifetimes, they shall have no liberation whatsoever.
Abandon evil association, O Lord, and preserve Your feet;
for without Your lotus feet, I see no other way.
Haridāsa finds his delight in the pair of feet [of the Lord], and he always loudly sings the *cintāmaṇi* jewel that is the name of Hari. HNC 3.92.
Thus ends the third chapter, titled "Description of Counterfeit Names," in the *Śrī Hari-nāma-cintāmaṇi*.
(4) Fourth Chapter.
Censuring the Name is equivalent to censuring the virtuous; since it constitutes the supreme offense against the Name, how could that which has attained renown tolerate its disparagement?
Victory to you, O life-breath of Gadādhara! Victory to you, O life of the Ganges!
Victory to you, Lord of Sītā, and to Śrīvāsa and all other devotees! HNC_4.1 //
The Lord said: "O Haridāsa, now explain in detail the offenses against the Name hereafter."
O servant of Hari, whatever strength the Lord bestows upon me, by His power I shall offer that very strength unto You. (HNC 4.3)
The ten kinds of offenses against the Name have been described in the scripture; I am greatly afraid of those very offenses. (HNC 4.4)
I am able to recount all [the offenses] one by one; let my strength fail me for having omitted these transgressions. (HNC 4.5)
Censuring the virtuous, regarding other deities as independent, and disparaging the Name, the reality, the Guru, the lineage, and the scripture. (HNC 4.6)
Meditation on the meaning of the name is merely a figurative construction;
for one who lacks faith, the offering of the name relies solely on the power of the name itself to destroy sin. (HNC 4.7)
The name "Kṛṣṇa" is equal to other auspicious deeds; yet to speak of it otherwise is an endless offense. (HNC 4.8)
These lapses are due to lack of attention;
the author of the Purāṇa attributes them to forceful negligence. (HNC 4.9)
Though one knows the greatness of Nāma, yet does not worship it, one sinks into the cycle of worldly existence through attachment to "I" and "mine. (HNC 4.10)
Blaming the saintly is the first offense;
knowing that blaming the saintly is the first offense, one realizes that through this offense, the living entity suffers total ruin. (HNC 4.11)

O Lord, you have spoken of two excellent characteristics— the essential nature (*svarūpa-lakṣaṇa*) and the circumstantial characteristic (*taṭastha-lakṣaṇa*)— in your deliberation with Uddhava in the eleventh book regarding the form of Kṛṣṇa, O All-pervading One. (HNC 4.12)
Compassionate, patient, equal toward all, and firm in a vow free from malice;
having truth as his essence, pure in soul, and devoted to the welfare of others. (HNC 4.13)
With an unshaken mind regarding sensual desires, self-controlled, possessing nothing, gentle, pure, moderate in eating, and tranquil in mind. (HNC 4.14)
Free from worldly striving, steadfast, firm with Kṛṣṇa as your sole refuge, vigilant, profoundly deep, and having conquered the six internal enemies. HNC_4.15 //
Free from pride, honoring others, skillful, and free from deceit—knowing one who possesses all these characteristics as a true saint (sādhu). // HNC_4.16 //
O Lord, all these characteristics are of two kinds; I shall now deliberate upon the distinction between the essential nature (*svarūpa*) and the extrinsic state (*taṭastha*). (HNC 4.17)
The essential characteristic (*svarūpa-lakṣaṇa*) is primarily characterized by taking exclusive shelter in Kṛṣṇa;
that which rests upon this [characteristic] is the incidental characteristic (*taṭastha-lakṣaṇa*).
Taking exclusive shelter in Kṛṣṇa is the essential characteristic.
In the definition of the indifferent (taṭastha-lakṣaṇa), there is the enumeration of other qualities.
By some stroke of fortune, one develops a taste for the company of the saintly;
they chant the name of Kṛṣṇa and take refuge at the feet of Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 4.19)
Its essential characteristic remained as it was;
yet, through constant singing, other qualities emerged within its name. (HNC 4.20)
Other multitudes of virtues are counted as merely incidental;
however, the essential union must certainly occur within the body of a Vaiṣṇava.
Saintliness is not found through the marks of caste and stage of life, nor by means of various types of dress;
the sole characteristic of a saint is taking exclusive refuge in Kṛṣṇa.

The arrangement of various appearances according to the marks of caste and stage of life is merely a construction; it is never taken into account as a defining characteristic of a saintly person. (HNC 4.22)
Taking refuge in Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the characteristic of a saintly person;
the chanting of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa is the boat for crossing over. (HNC 4.23)
In the divisions of householder, celibate student, forest-dweller, and renunciant;
and in the divisions of the groups of Śūdras, Vaiśyas, Kṣatriyas, and Brahmins. (HNC 4.24)
It has been determined that goodness never ceases;
the saint who takes exclusive refuge in Kṛṣṇa is so ordained by the scriptures. (HNC 4.25)
Having made service the defining characteristic of a householder-saint (gṛhi-sādhu) in Raghunāthadāsa,
this essence is placed as a crest-jewel upon the heads of householder-saints. (HNC 4.26)
Having become steady, go home; do not be a madman.
Gradually, step by step, cross over the ocean of worldly existence.
Abandoning the monkey-like state of detachment, show the world; enjoy sense objects as is appropriate, remaining unattached. (HNC 4.28)
Inwardly, one should reach the final goal; outwardly, one should engage in worldly affairs.
Before long, Śrī Kṛṣṇa will bring about your liberation.

"Furthermore, you possess the characteristic of a saintly person by having renounced the household; seeing this, they have embraced dispassion. Having imparted this instruction, it was an unprecedented hearing. (HNC 4.30)
One should not listen to vulgar stories, nor should one speak of vulgar matters; one should neither eat from a shared platter nor sit upon a shared platter. HNC 4.31.
O giver of honor, being free from pride, may I always chant the name of Kṛṣṇa;
and in Vraja, may I perform the service of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa within my mind. HNC_4.32 //
The householder and the renunciant—both possess the same essential nature and characteristics;
this essential nature and its characteristics are identical everywhere. Differences such as those of the stages of life (āśrama) are merely external designations. (HNC 4.33)
Even if one sees a person of wicked conduct who has no other refuge, he is nevertheless a virtuous and powerful one to be served by everyone in every way.
Therefore, one should always worship the words of Śrī Kṛṣṇa found in the Gītā and the Bhāgavatam with effort, according to all philosophical systems. (HNC 4.35)
This which exists here is a profound secret doctrine; by your grace, may I understand it so that I may attain the end. (HNC 4.36)

If a saint who has taken exclusive refuge in Kṛṣṇa reviles Him— whether due to the lingering scent of past sins or by taking past sins as a pretext— he becomes an offender against the Name; however, when he develops a taste for the Name of Kṛṣṇa, that [taste] will arise.
By reciting it even once, the evil committed in the past is destroyed.
The scent of former sins may remain for some days, but by the power of the name, it is gradually struck down and becomes exhausted. (HNC 4.38)
Quickly this foul odor of sin shall be dispelled; one becomes acquainted with the supreme nature of dharma. (HNC 4.39)
On some days that fragrance does not arise at all;
to ordinary people, it appears as a mass of evil. (HNC 4.40)
Having seen that very evil which consists of censuring the virtuous, one who has previously committed sins will again practice contempt. (HNC 4.41)
Such a person is indeed a heretic due to the fault of reviling a Vaiṣṇava;
he falls into the offense against the Name through the wrath of Kṛṣṇa.

Having attained the true characteristic of taking exclusive refuge in Kṛṣṇa, one should provide excellent proof [of that state]. Merely by singing the name of Kṛṣṇa with exclusive refuge in Him, one becomes well-acquainted with the names of the saints through the grace of Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 4.43)
No holy person has passed away this day except for a devotee of Kṛṣṇa;
I am a saintly man, but I am an incarnation of hypocrisy. (HNC 4.44)
In this concise and authoritative determination, I, the wretched one whose sole refuge is Kṛṣṇa, offer my salutations.
He in whose mouth the name of Kṛṣṇa resides is a saintly person. (HNC 4.45)
One should know that the grass has received a lowly tribute; one should consider the patient tree to have received justice. // HNC_4.46 //
He himself is free from pride, yet he bestows honor upon all;
the name of Kṛṣṇa from his mouth grants devotion to Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 4.47)
Indeed, the offense of mispronouncing the Name occurs when one hears even a single name from the mouth of a Vaiṣṇava saint, for Kṛṣṇa’s power resides within that saint’s body.
I shall offer my salutations to her, who is more powerful than even Viṣṇu.
The Vaiṣṇava is the spiritual master of the world and the friend of the universe;
the Vaiṣṇava is always an ocean of mercy toward all living beings.
And whoever utters such blasphemy against the Vaiṣṇavas will fall into hell for birth after birth. (HNC 4.50)
There is no other means for attaining devotion;
all living beings attain devotion through the grace of the Vaiṣṇavas. (HNC 4.51)
The body of a Vaiṣṇava remains permeated by the power of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; by touching that body, others develop devotion to Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 4.52)
The nectar from the lips of a Vaiṣṇava, the water from his feet, and the dust of a Vaiṣṇava’s feet—these three possess great power. HNC 4.53.
If one sits near a Vaiṣṇava while the Vaiṣṇava’s power is active, what are the symptoms?
The power of Kṛṣṇa emerges from the body. (HNC 4.54)
O Śakti, look upon me with faith in your heart;
let devotion arise and cause this body to tremble.
In the hearts of those who, with faith, dwell in the presence of a Vaiṣṇava, devotion shall arise. (HNC 4.56)
If, at the very first breath, one places the name of Kṛṣṇa upon the lips,
then by the power of that name, one shall obtain the entire collection of virtues.

Whatever faults one may attribute to a Vaiṣṇava, they amount to the fault of slandering a Vaiṣṇava; the faults of caste and previous karma are as good as destroyed. Only the remaining occasional faults remain in a Vaiṣṇava. He who slanders based on seeing such an occasional fault [commits this offense]. (HNC 4.58)
When faults have almost vanished, one may suffer insult; when the rod of Yama falls, one receives all suffering—this is entirely due to ignorance. (HNC 4.59)
The propagation of the greatness of the Name from the mouth of a Vaiṣṇava—O Kṛṣṇa, He cannot tolerate even the slightest censure of that Vaiṣṇava. (HNC 4.60)
Abandoning the sections on ritual law, yoga, sacrifice, and knowledge,
those who worship the name of Kṛṣṇa are supreme above all.
A true practitioner is one who takes refuge in the Name while remaining free from disparaging other deities or scriptures;
such a person does not engage in the censure of other deities or other scriptures, for they have taken refuge and dissolved their being in the Name, O pure holy ones. (HNC 4.62)
Whether he be a householder or a renunciant, it is well; one should strive to obtain the dust of his feet. (HNC 4.63)
Wherever there is delight in the Name, there indeed is the Vaiṣṇava;
such is the experience of the state of a Vaiṣṇava according to this method.
In this world, who—possessing caste, stage of life, wealth, scholarship, youth, beauty, strength, and followers—would not perform some purposeful action? (HNC 4.65)
Therefore, by means of the practice of *yoniśomanasikāra*, one should abandon the disparagement of the virtuous; this is the certainty of the Dharma. (HNC 4.66)
Pure devotion based on the Name takes the form of devotion to the devotee;
devoid of devotion to the devotee, O Haṭṭī, it is deformed. HNC 4.67.
Where there is censure of the saintly, there is no state of devotion;
therefore, such is the consequence of an offense. (HNC 4.68)
Abandoning the censuring of the saintly, one should practice devotion to the saints;
association with the saintly and service to the saintly—this is the practice of dharma. (HNC 4.69)
There are two kinds of association with the untruthful; among them, association with women is the very abandonment of such association— this is the conduct of a Vaiṣṇava.
In association with the wicked, there is boundless contempt for the saintly.
In all scriptures, there are two kinds of non-existence; of these two, one is association with women. (HNC 4.71)
One who associates with those who associate with women is counted among the common folk; O living being, you are truly blessed when you renounce attachment even to the celestial nymphs. HNC 4.72.
Those who remain within the dharma of matrimony in this worldly existence by the power of their own effort and the strength of their wives—
[not] by the force of false scriptures— for them [this applies]. (HNC 4.73)
One who is joined with unrighteousness, devoted to the company of women, and attached to female company is considered by people to be wicked according to the scriptures. (HNC 4.74)
The second type is the wicked (the non-devotee of Kṛṣṇa); there are three types of non-devotees of Kṛṣṇa— the wicked is the second type.
The proponent of illusionism, a mere bearer of the banner of Dharma, is a nihilist who denies the Lord.
By what power?
By the power of censuring all the world; by the power of censuring the virtuous, one avoids [all else], for this censure of the virtuous brings about the abandonment of all such associations.
In this world, those who are powerful through censure are to be avoided. (HNC 4.76)
Abandoning all these along with their company, take refuge in no other; by chanting the name of Kṛṣṇa, one attains the wealth of love for Kṛṣṇa.
A pseudo-Vaiṣṇava, a natural Vaiṣṇava,
one who is mostly a Vaiṣṇava, and a junior Vaiṣṇava— all these are one and the same thing.
One who worships while devoid of service to the saintly, yet possesses worldly faith, is a common Vaiṣṇava; such a person is merely a semblance of a Vaiṣṇava. (HNC 4.78)
One who merely resembles a Vaiṣṇava is not truly a Vaiṣṇava;
how can one obtain a true Vaiṣṇava through the company of saintly persons? (HNC 4.79)
Therefore, O Gaṇi, the younger and the middle [sons] are in the Tārā; indeed, the Vaiṣṇava is in the Tārā through the grace of Karibena. HNC_4.80 //
One should practice loving-kindness toward a neutral Vaiṣṇava, friendship toward a devotee of Kṛṣṇa,
compassion toward a fool, and indifference toward an enemy. (HNC 4.81)
One may be a middling devotee or a pure devotee;
by means of the name of Kṛṣṇa, one gains the right to perform spiritual advancement. (HNC 4.82)
The supreme Vaiṣṇava is one for whom the vision of Kṛṣṇa is the only nourishment everywhere;
for whom Kṛṣṇa is the abode of all things, and Kṛṣṇa is his very life and wealth. (HNC 4.83)
For him, there is no distinction between Vaiṣṇava and non-Vaiṣṇava;
he is the most excellent Vaiṣṇava, for whom the essence is the name of Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 4.84)
The intermediate Vaiṣṇava performs service to the saintly;
therefore, the noble intermediate Vaiṣṇava will certainly remain constantly engaged in the service of the saintly. (HNC 4.85)
Regarding the eligibility for the manifestation of the name of an ordinary Vaiṣṇava:
whoever is a devotee of a Vaiṣṇava is eligible for the manifestation of the name; such a person has mastered all the scriptures. (HNC 4.86)
The intermediate Vaiṣṇava is qualified to consider the offenses against the Name: "The intermediate Vaiṣṇava alone is qualified for the Name;
he shall consider the offenses regarding the worship of the Śrī-nāma. (HNC 4.87)
In the supreme Vaiṣṇava [tradition], an offense is impossible;
everywhere one perceives the threefold majesty of Kṛṣṇa.
Having reflected upon their respective duties, they avoided the offense of censuring the saintly. (HNC 4.89)
Excellent is association with the saintly, excellent is service, and excellent is the chanting of the Name;
compassion for all living beings—this is the conduct of a devotee. (HNC 4.90)

What should be done when censure of the virtuous occurs? Even if the reproach of the virtuous arises due to negligence, one should maintain remorse and take refuge at the feet of the virtuous. (HNC 4.91)
O Lord, forgive this offense;
grant the grace of Vaiṣṇava to these wicked revilers. HNC_4.92 //
O Great Compassionate One, you are truly virtuous; therefore, with a tender heart, forgive my offense and embrace me with your grace.
Now, let us consider the first offense;
I shall report it at the lotus feet according to your command. (HNC 4.94)
Those people who are bees at the lotus feet of Hari’s servant have the jewel of Hari’s name as their very life. (HNC 4.95)
Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled "An Examination of the Offense of Reviling Holy Men," in the *Śrī-Hari-nāma-cintāmaṇi*.
(5) Fifth Chapter.

Among the gods, the offense against the knowledge of Śiva’s sovereignty is that one who perceives with the intellect all the qualities, names, and so forth of the illustrious Viṣṇu as distinct from those of Śiva; such a person indeed brings harm to the name of Hari.
Victory to you, O Gadādhara, the life-breath of Jāhnavā!
Victory to you, Lord of Sītā; victory, O fair-complexioned one, to the devotees! HNC_5.1 //
O servant of Hari, having thus raised your hand to strike, listen now, O Lord of the Universe, to this second offense. (HNC 5.2)
Viṣṇu is the supreme non-dual reality and knowledge; Viṣṇu is the ultimate principle. He is the nature of consciousness, the Lord of the universe, eternally pure being. HNC 5.3.
From Kṛṣṇa, who wanders in Goloka, comes the essence of reality; He is adorned with the sixty-four qualities and is the reservoir of rasa.
The manifestation of the nature of Nārāyaṇa possesses sixty qualities;
those sixty qualities are the playful display of the universal Viṣṇu.
In the descent as a human being (puruṣāvatāra) and in the descent of his own partial incarnation (svāṃśāvatāra), those sixty qualities become manifest according to the specific activity. (HNC 5.6)
Viṣṇu is the undivided portion; the living entities are of two types of divided portions possessing fifty qualities.
Among these, Viṣṇu’s divided portions are of two kinds:
those with fifty qualities and those who are mere particles (bindus). (HNC 5.7)
The deities such as Giriśa are distinct partial manifestations (vibhinnāṃśa); ordinary living beings are not so.
These deities, such as Giriśa, are distinguished by fifty qualities; they are eternally endowed with these fifty qualities in a measure even greater than that. (HNC 5.8)
Beyond that, O Āra, when the five qualities are measured in their various portions, they are manifested through diverse arrangements. (HNC 5.9)
The state of Viṣṇu is sixty-fold; it is fully endowed with fifty-five qualities. It shines as Viṣṇu in all the scriptures—thus sing! HNC 5.10.
Beyond that, O Āra, the five qualities reside in Nārāyaṇa;
their existence is never found in any other being. (HNC 5.11)
In the sixth category is the Viṣṇu-tattva, the Supreme Lord;
Giriśa and other such deities are his servants. (HNC 5.12)
O Lord of the best of living beings, such as Śiva and others who are distinct portions [of You];
O Viṣṇu, Lord of all living beings, Lord of all gods! HNC 5.13.
To consider other deities together with Viṣṇu as equal, or to regard Viṣṇu as equal to other gods, is great ignorance; it is a failure to understand the true nature of the Lord. (HNC 5.14)
And in this inert world, Viṣṇu is the supreme Lord; Giriśa and the other gods are merely his executors. (HNC 5.15)
Someone says: "O Lord of the Three Heavens, the reality of Brahman, which possesses distinctions, is always equal within the three qualities of Māyā. (HNC 5.16)
Among the various doctrines and counter-arguments of the established scriptures, O venerable Nārāyaṇa, you are the ultimate conclusion;
you are the cause of the creation and dissolution of Brahmā and Śiva. (HNC 5.17)
Whoever worships another deity while abandoning Vāsudeva,
having abandoned the Lord, that person sinks into the cycle of worldly existence.
Some say that Viṣṇu is the supreme reality, knowing him to be so and accepting the Vedic statements that the entire universe is pervaded by Viṣṇu. (HNC 5.19)
Therefore, Viṣṇu is the presiding presence in every deity;
in the worship of all deities, Viṣṇu is equal to them all.
O friend, understand this statement, which is primarily prohibitive, as an injunction:
this is the prohibition against the worship of other deities. (HNC 5.21)
In this entire universe which is composed entirely of Viṣṇu, by performing worship of Viṣṇu, the worship of all the gods is accomplished. (HNC 5.22)
If water is given at the root of a tree, there is joy for the branches;
if water is poured upon the sprouts, it leads to the destruction of the tree. (HNC 5.23)
Therefore, having worshipped Viṣṇu, one should abandon other deities; yet, for the sake of those very [other] deities, one has worshipped them. (HNC 5.24)
This method is approved by the gods for long days;
this modern method is abandoned when the ripening of karma is difficult. (HNC 5.25)
In the Kali age, when the defects of the doctrine of illusion (māyāvāda) have arrived, when many gods are worshipped, and when Viṣṇu is viewed as being no different from them; HNC_5.26 //
Each individual deity is the giver of a single fruit;
Viṣṇu is the giver of all fruits and the protector of all.
If those possessed by desire were able to know the ultimate reality, they would abandon other deities and obtain the fruit of worshipping Viṣṇu. (HNC 5.28)
The prescribed duties for a Vaiṣṇava householder:
Whoever among householders is a devotee of Viṣṇu should perform all activities while worshipping Kṛṣṇa, setting aside all doubt. (HNC 5.29)
O Kṛṣṇa, since the purificatory rites beginning with conception and ending at the cremation ground are performed according to the Vedic mantras, one should worship Him accordingly. HNC 5.30.
Viṣṇu indeed is the worship of the Vaiṣṇava; this is the rule declared in the Vedas.
O Kṛṣṇa, the offering of the remains of the worship (nirmālya) is to be given to the host of gods and ancestors. HNC 5.31.
In the doctrine of the Māyāvādins, whoever performs the ancestral śrāddha rite or worships other deities dies due to that transgression. (HNC 5.32)
To harbor a dualistic perception regarding the reality of Viṣṇu is an offense; by that offense, devotion is obstructed. (HNC 5.33)
O Lord, among the hosts of deities beginning with Śiva, there is a distinct offense against the Name that is terrifying. (HNC 5.34)
Since Viṣṇu’s power is the supreme power, O Lord, the Siddhānta system maintains that power is distinct [from its possessor]. (HNC 5.35)
O Śiva, Brahmā, Gaṇapati, Sūrya, and the Guardians of the Quarters; O Kṛṣṇa, Śakti, and Bala; O Lord, for a long time! HNC_5.36 //
Therefore, the Supreme Lord alone is to be known;
all other gods are reckoned as being within His power. (HNC 5.37)
Therefore, in every undertaking, having abandoned the state of inertness regarding action, the householder should attain devotion and the true disposition. (HNC 5.38)

O Vaiṣṇava, what indeed is the duty of a householder? It consists of maintaining devotion with a pure heart, performing sacred rites, and offering the remains of the offerings (nirmālya) to satisfy the hosts of gods and ancestors. (HNC 5.39)
One should avoid performing worship of many gods and goddesses;
all devotees of Kṛṣṇa should perform the offering of oblations (tarpaṇa). // HNC_5.40 //
In the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and His Vaiṣṇavas, one obtains all fruits; there is no offense regarding the Name—chant the Name always. (HNC 5.41)
O assembly of humans in the world, conduct the way of life according to the four castes; practicing the duties of your respective castes, proceed upon the path of the dharma of life. HNC 5.42.
Due to the confusion of castes caused by the lowest-born, all those of low birth have abandoned their base duties; they always perform the conduct of Śūdras and the worldly activities of saṃsāra.
The mixed castes, the outcastes, and the Thākībeḳas follow the conduct of Śūdras; apart from these four varṇas, there is no other dharma in this world. (HNC 5.44)

A worldly person, having sustained their livelihood through the duties of their respective caste, should cultivate devotion on the path of bhakti; the four castes should perform their caste duties within the world, for by the power of pure Kṛṣṇa-bhakti, one attains virtuous conduct. (HNC 5.45)
Even if one belongs to the four castes, if they do not worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa, they remain within the duties and conduct of their caste and sink into the Raurava hell. (HNC 5.46)
Without the duties of one's caste (varṇa), there is no dharma for a householder; all the activities of a householder consist of the practice of the duties of their caste. HNC 5.47.
One should maintain one's livelihood within the duties of one's caste;
for the sake of acquiring necessary means, one should worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa. HNC 5.48.
Those men who, by their very nature, have reached the limit of scriptural injunctions, should pay heed to the fulfillment of their own caste-duties. (HNC 5.49)
This exposition of the principles known as bhakti-yoga consists of authoritative statements regarding the doctrine of the arising of ecstatic emotion within bhakti-yoga. (HNC 5.50)
When a state of being arises, there is no injunction and no activity; when the task has arisen through that state, the maintenance of the body is accomplished. (HNC 5.51)
This is the practice of non-duality for the householder Vaiṣṇava;
it is the cessation of duality within the non-dual reality of Śrī Viṣṇu. HNC 5.52.
The name and the named, the quality and the possessor of quality—though they are non-different, the knowledge of Viṣṇu is pure; there is but one story for the removal of duality:
Viṣṇu’s name, Viṣṇu’s form, and the multitude of Viṣṇu’s qualities. (HNC 5.53)
Viṣṇu never possesses a form separate from Himself; He is non-dual, indivisible, all-pervading, and consists of pure consciousness. (HNC 5.54)
O horse of ignorance, if there is the affliction of duality,
then even the semblance of the Name will be impossible for one lacking love.
Through the grace of the true guru, that misfortune is destroyed;
with each successive act of devotion, the light of the pure Name shines forth.
The fallacious reasoning of the proponents of Māyā is an offense;
through the knowledge of one's own philosophical tenets, duality arises as an activity. It is an offense, not its cessation. (HNC 5.57)
O Bali, according to the proponents of Māyā, Brahman is the supreme reality—without distinction, without change, formless, and pure being. HNC 5.58.
The form of Viṣṇu and the name of Viṣṇu are fashioned by Māyā; when Māyā disappears, Viṣṇu ceases to exist and one becomes absorbed in Brahman. HNC 5.59.
All these fallacious arguments are merely a nihilistic doctrine of truth;
they are a negligence resulting from the absence of the recognition of all-pervasive power within the supreme reality. (HNC 5.60)
He who possesses power is Brahman; he is indeed Viṣṇu.
The dispute regarding their names is merely that; the Vedas provide the final determination.
Viṣṇu is related to the reality of Brahman;
Viṣṇu is the supreme reality, whose nature is both devoid of attributes (nirviśeṣa-dharma) and possessed of attributes (saviśeṣa-dharma)—these two are one and the same essence. (HNC 5.62)
Viṣṇu possesses inconceivable power that shatters all opposition; effortlessly, he establishes beauty in the hand of the hand. (HNC 5.63)
The notion of a living soul (jīva) is by its very nature exceedingly slight;
it is an inconceivable power that does not fall within the range of the ordinary mind.
If one establishes God as a single entity for the sake of one's own intellect, then in that fragmented knowledge, the reality of Brahman becomes inferior. (HNC 5.65)
Viṣṇu, worshipped by the gods, abandoned his supreme station; Brahmā was bound like a horse and did not understand what is beneficial or harmful. (HNC 5.66)
When one understands and realizes the knowledge of the nature consisting of consciousness,
one regards Viṣṇu and the names and qualities of Viṣṇu as one.
O pure embodiment of knowledge, O Śrī-Kṛṣṇa! Having attained the realization of our relationship, I worship Your name and form. HNC 5.68.

Whether it be Śiva or Viṣṇu, one should cultivate the realization of non-difference; for this sense of difference exists only in respect to insentient names, forms, and qualities—it does not exist in the principle of Consciousness, as that is its very nature. (HNC 5.69)
In the reality of Viṣṇu, the knowledge of difference is a harmful transformation;
in the reality of Śiva, the difference from Viṣṇu is utterly beyond consideration.

The conduct and activities of the devotees and the Māyāvādīs differ; the great devotees take refuge in devotion alone as their singular goal, worshipping the one Lord Kṛṣṇa and abandoning all other beings. (HNC 5.71)
One should not engage in the censure of other deities or other scriptures; one should worship and honor others as being powerful servants of Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 5.72)
Every day, by offering the remains of food (nirmālya) to the household deity,
one performs the act of satiation for the gods, the ancestors, and all living beings.
In whatever way other gods may grant their vision, a servant of Kṛṣṇa offers them worship with offerings. (HNC 5.74)
If the hosts of Māyāvādins perform the worship of Viṣṇu, yet do not distribute the *prasāda* and *nirmālya* to their devotees, they shall fear dissolution. (HNC 5.75)
The proponent of illusion (māyāvādī) is an offender against the name of Hari; Hari does not accept the worship offered by him. (HNC 5.76)
Accepting the remains of offerings made to other deities is an offense;
it always acts as an obstacle to the practice of pure devotion. (HNC 5.77)
Then, if a pure devotee, having worshiped Śrī Kṛṣṇa, performs worship to another deity and offers him the prasāda [of Kṛṣṇa], [he commits an offense]. (HNC 5.78)
In accepting that grace there is no fault; in worshipping the deity in that form there is no obstruction to devotion. (HNC 5.79)
One who is a pure devotee is never an offender;
having attained love through the Name, they bestow victory upon the Name. (HNC 5.80)
Although the remedy for this offense may be the knowledge of Viṣṇu through negligence, one should instead practice meditation on the true nature of Viṣṇu with repentance. (HNC 5.81)
By remembering Śrī Viṣṇu, one's offenses are destroyed; even if one sees another [offender], no offense occurs through such effort. HNC 5.82.
O Kṛṣṇa, friend of forgiveness, virtue, and devotion; ocean of compassion, sea of forbearance! HNC_5.83 //
I shall avoid the company of those who serve many gods;
I shall perform worship of the one Lord, the Vaiṣṇava.
Those people who have devotion to the feet of Haridāsa Pāda have the *Harināma-cintāmaṇi* as their very life. (HNC 5.85)
Thus ends the fifth chapter, titled "The Offense of Ignorance Regarding the Independence [of the Lord] in Other Deities," in the *Śrī Hari-nāma-cintāmaṇi*.
(6) Sixth Chapter.
Disrespect toward the guru,
disrespect toward the guru— conquer, conquer the five principles, O Śrī Rādhā-Mādhava!
Victory to Navadvīpa, Vraja, the Yamunā, and the Vaiṣṇavas!
O Hari’s servant, the Lord has made this submission:
this occurrence, in this form, is called the third offense. (HNC 6.2)
O Lord, by your command, I have committed many offenses and all manner of transgressions against my teacher. (HNC 6.3)
Having wandered through many wombs, this human body is difficult to obtain, exceedingly auspicious,
and yet it is impermanent and full of suffering.
As long as one remains alive. // HNC_6.4 //
If one does not strive to attain the supreme auspiciousness,
it will be lost again; this body is impermanent.
Having obtained food, he died. // HNC_6.5 //
Having obtained this human body, which is so difficult to find within the cycle of worldly existence,
a transmigrating soul must inevitably take refuge in a true guru.
Taking refuge in the Guru as a helmsman,
one crosses over by means of favor toward Kṛṣṇa.
Śānta, the characteristics of a devotee of Kṛṣṇa are such that when the guru, with humble words,
brings him satisfaction, he receives the initiation of Kṛṣṇa and absorption in Him.
By which one crosses to the further shore of saṃsāra.
In the state of *sahaja*, the living being’s mind is already fixed on Kṛṣṇa; it is only through vain logic that this is lost. Abandoning such discursive reasoning, take refuge in right understanding.
One who hates the guru obtains the mantra. // HNC_6.8 //
A householder living among the multitude of living beings, remaining within the system of social classes and stages of life (varṇāśrama), should take refuge in a true guru;
if one remains as a worthy recipient (sat-pātra) within the higher classes such as the Brāhmaṇas, they will become fit for this path.
O Brāhmaṇa teacher, if one among all castes possesses devotion to Kṛṣṇa, [he is the best]. (HNC 6.9)
In the absence of a worthy recipient within the Brahmin caste,
one may receive initiation from another caste; it is appropriate for a high-caste person to accept a teacher from such a lineage.
For the examination of the teacher and the disciple. // HNC_6.10 //
In consideration of caste, reflection upon a worthy recipient is more meritorious;
one who knows the truth of Kṛṣṇa is a true spiritual master, even if he is born of low birth.
Whether one is a brahmin, a śūdra, a householder, or a renunciant—O Guru, you are the wish-fulfilling tree. HNC_6.11 //
In the ultimate sense, the consideration of caste and the recipient is of little importance;
the constant purpose is the meeting with a worthy vessel.
And if this delight were pure, // HNC_6.12 //
The primary purpose for obtaining a worthy recipient is pure gold; through that,
one attains union with the higher caste.
By which [merit], one attains good fortune and gold. // HNC_6.13 //
If one who has renounced the household life takes refuge with a non-householder guru for any reason whatsoever, he abandons the householder’s duty and enters another stage of life.
Then, having attained the ultimate truth, you should seek out a virtuous teacher for the remainder.
In that fortnight, having received initiation and instruction from those teachers who uphold all the systems praised by the Ācāryas, that person—
It shines in the nectar of the essence of names. // HNC_6.15 //
If one has already abandoned the household life after practicing devotion as a householder, there is no need to abandon the original guru; however, if a householder devotee attains dispassion,
he may leave worldly life according to the prescribed injunctions.
Therefore, one should take refuge at the feet of the previous guru for as long as life lasts.
If a householder is praised as a spiritual teacher among householders, it is because he is a pure devotee; otherwise,
he would not be a suitable person for that role.
Every moment is suitable for the yoga of the Guru. // HNC_6.17 //
Having found a true guru, one should worship him; when worship is performed,
the dawn of devotion arises,
and through detachment from worldly existence, one abandons saṃsāra.
When one becomes dispassionate, then— // HNC_6.18 //
One who, by means of the renunciant stage of life (vairāgya-āśrama), makes the three types of renunciants his gurus,
shall become a renunciant person (tyāgī-puruṣa) upon taking up the renunciant stage of life; such a one is a guru.
At his feet, the peacock [of passion] has become dispassionate;
he is the Guru, the wish-fulfilling tree of instruction. (HNC 6.19)

It is necessary to show equal respect to both initiation (dīkṣā) and instruction (śikṣā), as well as to the two types of gurus; though initiation and instruction differ, one must honor both gurus equally.
O noble one, drink this wealth of the ultimate truth without effort, if you so desire. HNC_6.20 //
The one who gives the Kṛṣṇa-name mantra is the initiation-guru;
the one who gives the reality is the instruction-guru; and the Vaiṣṇava is the instruction-guru of all. Destroy [all other gurus].
The progenitor of all that is auspicious.
In the Sādhu Sampradāya, all Ācāryas are established as gurus of instruction; one should practice by taking refuge in the instructions of the original guru of the tradition.
To the primordial teacher, the crown jewel of gurus, he offered worship in the appropriate manner.
If one follows his well-established doctrine,
there is no need for any other instruction;
one should strive to receive his command.
There is no other initiation like this one.
One should perform the formal selection of a lineage-teacher (sampradāya-guru);

among the assembly of lineage-teachers, one should recognize the instructional teacher (śikṣā-guru). One should not consider the instruction of a scholar belonging to another school as authoritative. (HNC 6.24)
One who is well-disciplined, virtuous, and of good conduct, always knowing what is appropriate for initiation and being truly wise, is a fit *guru*. (HNC 6.25)

If one receives the Kṛṣṇa-mantra from a Māyāvādin, there is no attainment of the ultimate truth; in the opinion of the Māyāvādin, the Kṛṣṇa-mantra exists [only nominally], and thus he never attains the supreme goal. (HNC 6.26)
One should not accept anyone other than a pure devotee as one's guru; such an act is unjust.
Whoever gives such instruction and whoever receives it—both shall go to hell and find no means of deliverance. (HNC 6.27)
One who abandons pure devotion and engages in argumentative debate—his entire life is nothing but a contradiction. (HNC 6.28)
How can one who is himself unperfected rescue living beings? How could he bestow any auspiciousness upon others? (HNC 6.29)
