Therefore, for those pure devotees who serve with humility, the one they approach becomes their suitable guru, as stated in all the scriptures. (HNC 6.30)
The guru’s essential nature is initiation; the guru’s instruction is service to Kṛṣṇa. In him, the splendor of the power of Kṛṣṇa and the people of Vraja shines forth. (HNC 6.31)
One should never perceive the guru as an ordinary living being;
the guru is the power of Kṛṣṇa, eternally the Lord most dear to Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 6.32)
One who always possesses this intelligence and practices devotion to the guru crosses over the cycle of worldly existence by the power of that devotion to the guru.
First is the worship of the guru, and after that is the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa;
one should offer the prasāda of Śrī Kṛṣṇa to the guru, who is the Lord. (HNC 6.34)
Having received the command of the Guru, one should worship Kṛṣṇa with effort; remembering the venerable Guru, one should offer Kṛṣṇa into the mouth. HNC 6.35.
Faith is appropriate toward that which is venerable;
for those who show contempt for what is venerable, their transgression constitutes an obstacle to their devotion. (HNC 6.36)
One who practices equal devotion toward the Guru, Kṛṣṇa, and the Vaiṣṇavas, and takes refuge in the Name as a pure devotee, shall quickly cross over. (HNC 6.37)
Whosoever possesses unshakable faith in the hand [of the Guru], by the power of the pure Name, they obtain the wealth of divine love. (HNC 6.38)
If at any time such an event should occur while one is about to abandon the guru in that place—
the worthiness of the guru being diminished by association with the wicked— HNC 6.39.
In the first [case], there are three [stages]; the sixth is the preeminent guru.
In the subsequent offense, one is struck; knowledge is destroyed.
One who harbors hatred toward a Vaiṣṇava abandons the nectar of the Name;
gradually, his wealth is destroyed and he falls under the power of lustful women. (HNC 6.41)
Leaving aside one's own guru, a disciple may, through the grace of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, obtain a true guru and again chant the pure Name. (HNC 6.42)

Prior to the relationship between teacher and disciple, there must be mutual examination; the teacher shall inflict punishment upon unworthy disciples, and by serving an unworthy teacher, the disciple becomes a fool. (HNC 6.43)
Since the stability of the relationship between the two has been lost for some time, abandon their mutual connection at once. (HNC 6.44)
Having examined a pure guru and chosen him as one's teacher, if one acts with contempt toward that true guru,
such a person is the most sinful offender throughout the entire cycle of existence.
Therefore, one should first make a special effort toward pure devotion, which is excellent in the form of the Guru, appearing as a friend. (HNC 6.46)
One for whom the hardship of abandoning the guru never arises—by contemplating him in such a form, one will never fall into danger. (HNC 6.47)
Just as a guru generally cannot deliver a disciple who is devoid of devotion, for this very reason one should seek a pure guru after thorough examination. (HNC 6.48)
Disrespect toward the true guru is a terrifying offense; by this offense, both gods and men are ruined. (HNC 6.49)
The procedure for serving the Guru consists of [attending to] the Guru’s bed, seat, sandals, and other vehicles;
his footstool; the water used for his ablutions; and avoiding stepping on his shadow. (HNC 6.50)
One should perform salutation to the Guru, who stands before one as the embodiment of other forms of worship, non-dual knowledge, initiation, exposition, sovereignty, and so forth. HNC 6.51.
In whatever manner one beholds the Guru,
one should prostrate like a staff upon the ground and perform salutation.
One should utter the name of the Guru with devotion;
one should never disregard the Guru’s command. (HNC 6.53)
One must certainly practice service with devotion to the guru;
one must never speak words that are displeasing to the guru. (HNC 6.54)
One should take refuge at the feet of the guru with humility; one should always perform actions that are dear to the guru. HNC 6.55.
O Lord, by the power of Your multitude of Vedic hymns, all perfections are attained through conduct such as this and the congregational chanting of Kṛṣṇa’s name. HNC 6.56.
If one should harbor contempt for the Guru, or take refuge in the company of the wicked, or in the views of corrupt scriptures; HNC_6.57 //
Then, casting aside both that company and those scriptures,
I shall lament at the feet of that very Guru.
May the compassionate Guru show mercy and grant love for the Name; he is indeed a merciful Vaiṣṇava. (HNC 6.59)
For one who is saturated with the dust of the feet of Hari’s servant, even the name of the wish-fulfilling gem is but ashes, more worthless than a blade of grass. (HNC 6.60)
Thus ends the sixth chapter, titled "Consideration of Disrespect toward the Guru," in the *Śrī Hari-nāma-cintāmaṇi*.
(7) Seventh Chapter.
Victory, victory to Gadādhara and Gaurāṅga, the eternal bliss!
Victory to the Lord of Sītā, victory to the multitude of Gaura’s devotees! HNC_7.1 //
O servant of Hari, O powerful one, this is the fourth offense:
the reviling of the Vedas and scriptures, and the obstruction of the nectar of devotion. (HNC 7.2)
The traditional scriptures—the Śrutis, the Śāstras, the Vedas, the Upaniṣads, and the Purāṇas—are the sole authority;
indeed, everything is the breath of Kṛṣṇa and is authoritative everywhere. (HNC 7.3)
Especially when knowledge arises regarding the extraordinary reality,
then all the traditions and their perfected adepts become devoted to it.
The reality that transcends the insentient is beyond the range of the senses;
without the grace of Kṛṣṇa, it is not within their reach. (HNC 7.5)
Incapacity of the instruments, delusion, desire to deceive, and negligence—these four faults arise everywhere in human cognition. (HNC 7.6)
O Veda-catuṣṭaya, you are free from all defects;
without the Vedas, there is no way to reach the ultimate truth. HNC_7.7 //
O Kṛṣṇa, having shown great compassion to the living beings bound by illusion,
You bestowed the Veda, the Purāṇas, and other scriptures, possessing the wisdom of the seers.

These ten root disciplines (śikṣā) are the traditional teachings; they are the principles of the objects of knowledge found within the scriptures of revelation (śruti). They consist of the distribution of both action (karma) and knowledge (jñāna).
One attains the essence of them all through pure devotion alone. (HNC 7.9)
O deluded soul, having purified both action and knowledge through Māyā, Hari has instructed you in the authority of pure devotion. HNC_7.10 //

By means of the instruments of valid cognition (*pramāṇa*), the Vedic statements are the means of knowledge (*nayaṭī*); the connection, the purpose, and the subject matter are the objects of knowledge (*prameya*). (HNC 7.11)
O Essence of the Ten Roots! Destroy ignorance and bring forth the light of true knowledge for the living being. HNC_7.12 //
1. Hari is the singular supreme reality; 2. the three are all-possessing of power; 3. the three are the embodiments of aesthetic flavor.
In the first [syllable], *śikhāya*, there is the Supreme Reality, the one Hari, dark-complexioned, omnipotent, and bearing the form of aesthetic essence (*rasa*). (HNC 7.13)
It ordains the supreme bliss of the living soul;
it is the eternal substratum that sustains the stars within the firmament.
These three are the objects of knowledge concerning Śrī Kṛṣṇa: the imparting of Vedic and scriptural instruction into the hearts of living beings. (HNC 7.15)
4. Regarding the second, the principle of the individual soul (*jīva-tattva*): it is a distinct portion of the *śikhā*;
it consists of infinite, atomic units of consciousness (*cit-paramāṇu*). (HNC 7.16)

5. Nitya-baddha and 6. Nitya-mukta: there are two kinds of living beings (jīvas) distinguished as eternally bound and eternally liberated. Their existence fills the entire expanse of the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa). HNC_7.17 //
O bound soul,
O bound soul, you who have turned away from Kṛṣṇa out of attachment to illusion,
you experience pleasure and pain within the infinite universe of Brahmāṇḍa. (HNC 7.18)
The liberated souls are eternally free; they worship Kṛṣṇa as the attendants of Kṛṣṇa,
and in the supreme realm, they enjoy the abundance of the wealth of love.
This very subject—the soul—is the object of my inquiry;
by receiving instruction from the Vedas and the scriptures, one becomes a servant of Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 7.20)
7. The inconceivable relationship of difference-and-non-difference is the operation of consciousness;
the operation of the insentient is entirely of the nature of inconceivable difference-and-non-difference. (HNC 7.21)
All things, whether sentient or insentient, consist of the power of Kṛṣṇa;
how can there be an inconceivable distinction or non-distinction between them according to the Śruti and the Śāstras? (HNC 7.22)
O Jīva, by this knowledge you shall know: "I am the servant of Kṛṣṇa;
Kṛṣṇa is my eternal Lord, the light of the sun of consciousness. (HNC 7.23)

By the power of the Vedas and Śāstras, which consist solely of the transformation of [divine] potency, one should avoid the deceit of censuring the Veda through corrupted views such as the theory of illusory manifestation (vivarta). (HNC 7.24)
The knowledge of the relationship between these seven categories of objects of cognition is itself that knowledge of the relationship;
the instruction on the scriptures of the Śruti is most worthy of being adopted. (HNC 7.25)
Furthermore, Śikṣādeva understood the essence of what is to be expressed:
the ninefold method of devotion to Kṛṣṇa, beginning with *rāgānugā*. (HNC 7.26)
8. The subject matter—ninefold devotion:
hearing, chanting, remembering, worshiping, bowing down, serving, servitude, friendship, and self-surrender. (HNC 7.27)
Among the various types of devotion, the Name is the essence of all;
the Vedas proclaim the greatness of the Praṇava. (HNC 7.28)
9. Having taken refuge in pure devotion characterized by love for Kṛṣṇa as its sole purpose, a human being attains the opulence of love through the power of Kṛṣṇa’s grace. (HNC 7.29)
The offense of disparaging the teachings of the Vedas is one of these nine objects of knowledge; the Vedas serve as the authoritative means of proof.
A guru who is conversant with the reality of the Vedas provides the necessary connection.
And that person who utters such blasphemy is a most base man, an offender against the Name; so says the Śruti. (HNC 7.31)
Jaimini, Kapila, the naked Nāstika, Sugata, and Gautama— these six persons are devoted to the doctrine of causal reasoning that contradicts the Vedas. (HNC 7.32)
Although the Veda is held as authoritative in its opening sections, O Lord, it does not acknowledge You;
Jaimini proclaims that the Karma-kāṇḍa is supreme, as he explains in his *Bālakī*. (HNC 7.33)
The existence of Īśvara is unestablished according to Kapila’s conception; yet, even if one accepts Yoga, the meaning cannot be understood. (HNC 7.34)
They spread the Tāmasa principles of nakedness and propagate a religion that contradicts the Vedas. (HNC 7.35)
The nihilist Cārvākas never accept the Vedas;
the Sugatas, the Buddhists, explain it in one way. (HNC 7.36)
I do not worship Īśvara as the author of Gautama’s Nyāya; for according to the doctrine of that [system], he is included among mere human beings. (HNC 7.37)
All these various philosophical systems involve the censure of the Śruti; all these wicked doctrines revile the Vedas.
The wise understand this, sometimes explicitly and sometimes implicitly. (HNC 7.38)
All these, by their very nature, are offenders; therefore, one must certainly renounce them all. (HNC 7.39)
The doctrine of Māyāvāda is extremely wicked; abandon all these false views that contradict the Vedas, including Māyāvāda itself.
Only through pure devotion can one experience [the Truth] beyond dispute. (HNC 7.40)
The doctrine of Māyā is a false scripture, a hidden Buddhist view; it is a distortion of the meaning of the Vedas, accepted in this age of Kali. (HNC 7.41)
Umāpati manifested himself in the form of a brahmin;
having recognized him as Tāmara, they made him their preceptor.
O Jaimini, you who accept only the Veda as the source for the nature [of things], explain the world through the meaning of the unmodified revelation. HNC_7.43 //
The Guru, a proponent of the doctrine of illusion (māyāvādī), established the Buddhist dharma within the Vedic scriptures and concealed the core essence of devotion. (HNC 7.44)
All these various philosophical doctrines depart far from devotion;
by the name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the living entity incurs offense.
In the investigation of the scriptures, the pure method is that the scripture employs the function of direct denotation (*abhidhā*) to bring about union;
thus the living being attains pure devotion and the wealth of love. (HNC 7.46)
In the Veda there is metaphorical indication (*lakṣaṇā*), and in the hand there is an improper manner;
one who goes far from eternal truth perishes through that transgression. (HNC 7.47)
The name of Kṛṣṇa is the *praṇava* (Om) honored by all the Vedas; by that name alone, every living being attains the eternal abode. (HNC 7.48)
The Mahāvākya is the name of Kṛṣṇa derived from the Praṇava; therein alone is the eternal repose of the fortunate devotee. (HNC 7.49)
In every philosophical system, it is established that the world, which is the manifestation of names, is the very nature of the power of the Veda known as Cit. HNC 7.50.

To teach the practice of exclusive, pure name-worship is the instruction of all the Vedas; those who do not accept this are considered unfortunate, for they commit an offense against the Name by slandering the Vedas. (HNC 7.51)
Those great souls who are devoted solely to the name, which is pure and rests upon the Vedas, obtain the wealth of love for the nectar of the Name. HNC 7.52.
All the power of the Vedas is contained within the essence of Hari’s name;
one shall obtain supreme love and boundless bliss. HNC_7.53 //
Furthermore, O Bala, know that for those great beings who have been liberated,
the constant chanting of the Name is held in their hands within the supreme ether.

In the Kali Yuga, people follow the teachings of *tāmasa* tantras which contradict the Vedas; they worship the illusory power (*māyā-śakti*) of the masses and abandon the nectar of the conscious Self, the Supreme Person named Kṛṣṇa. (HNC 7.55)
Those who uphold the *tāmasika* tantras revile the revealed scriptures (*śruti*);
taking pleasure in liquor and meat, they die through unrighteousness.
They all do not obtain the name of Kṛṣṇa;
they never obtain the abode of Vṛndāvana, which belongs to Kṛṣṇa.
The goddess Māyā has sincere compassion as her sole purpose;
through the goddess Māyā, all heretics attain the lower realms, for she bestows the nectar of her name while having no intention of granting it [to others]. (HNC 7.58)
Therefore, O Māyā, if you are pleased by service to the saintly, then grant me,
who am free from deceit, the shade of Kṛṣṇa’s feet.
Māyā is a servant of Kṛṣṇa; she metes out punishment to those whose senses are turned outward.
If Māyā is worshipped, one receives no auspiciousness; it is a vessel of misfortune.
O Kṛṣṇa, upon whomsoever the Goddess of Māyā bestows the name,
she acts with sincere compassion and leads them across the shore of worldly existence.
Therefore, abandon the offense of reviling the Śruti and immerse yourself day after day in the aesthetic relish of chanting the Name. (HNC 7.62)
Even if one should commit an offense against it through negligence— thereby incurring the censure of the Śruti—
if one feels remorse, one may again offer veneration to that Śruti. (HNC 7.63)
O assembly of Vedas, I shall always worship you with effort, offering you flowers and *tulasī* along with the *Bhāgavata*.
O Kṛṣṇa, incarnation of the essence of the Bhāgavata scriptures, please show me boundless compassion; you must certainly do so. HNC_7.65 //
For those who have taken up the weight of the dust from the feet of Haridāsa, the wish-fulfilling jewel named "Hāra" is placed around their necks. HNC_7.66
Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "Consideration of the Offense of Slandering the Vedas," in the *Śrī Hari-nāma-cintāmaṇi*.
(8) The Eighth Chapter.
Victory to You, O Gaura Gadādhara Śrī Rādhā-Mādhava, whose speech regarding the Name is thus meaningful;
victory to the Gaṅgā, the ground of Gaura’s pastimes, and to the Vaiṣṇavas! HNC_8.1 //
O Lord, Son of Śacī, to conceptualize and contemplate the meaning of Hari’s name is the fifth offense. (HNC 8.2)
The greatness of the Name has been declared by Smṛti; through playfulness and faith, one attains absorption in the Name.
O Kṛṣṇa, having shown mercy, deliver me with a compassionate heart. HNC_8.3 //
There is no knowledge like that of Nāma; there is no purity like that of Nāma.
There is no vow like that of Nāma; there is no strength like that of Nāma.
In this world, there is no meditation equal to name;
in any view, there is no fruit equal to name.
There is no form of renunciation equal to Nāma;
there has never been anything equal to Nāma. (HNC 8.6)
In this world, there is no merit equal to that of Nāma;
nor, upon reflection, can one find a destiny equal to that of Nāma.
The Name is supreme liberation; the Name is the highest state. The Name is supreme peace; the Name is the highest station.
In the Name alone is supreme devotion; in the Name is pure intellect;
in the Name is supreme love; in the Name is the highest mindfulness. (HNC 8.9)
The name is the causal reality; the name is the Lord of all. The name is the supreme object of worship, the all-pervading one in the form of the Guru. (HNC 8.10)
The name Kṛṣṇa is the most supreme of all;
one thousand names of Viṣṇu are equal to a single name of Rāma;
and one name of Kṛṣṇa is equal to those three names of Rāma.
The meaning of *Nāma* is such that descent into hell becomes inevitable;
the multitude of scriptures always sing the majesty of *Nāma*.
Through the power of the *cittattva* (consciousness-principle) of *Nāma*, the world comes to know it. HNC 8.12.
If those who are powerful heretics were to treat as mere figurative praise (arthavāda) the fruits of the names revealed in the Śruti and Smṛti, [it would be a grave error]. (HNC 8.13)
Those base individuals who treat the name of Hari as a mere figurative eulogy are the most sinful;
they shall perish, being cooked again and again in hell. (HNC 8.14)
O fool, bring the fruit of the hearing of the Name into reality;
once a taste for the Name has been given, from that alone shall the fruit arise.
The purport of the scripture is the welfare and non-welfare of the living being; the base one does not know this, but understands it perversely. (HNC 8.16)
The fruit of name is truth;
therefore, there is no purpose for the discourse on meaning,
as the ritual section (karma-kāṇḍa) is merely deceitful knowledge for one's own self-interest.
In the reality of devotion, such things do not exist. HNC 8.17.
Know that the scriptural declarations of rewards in the section on ritual action (karma-kāṇḍa) are intended merely to attract people;
however, in the reality of devotion (bhakti-tattva), the declarations of reward are considered eternally true.
There is no place for deceit regarding the truth, nor is there ever any room for falsehood; there is no self-interest in renunciation, for it is called giving. (HNC 8.19)
The explanatory praise regarding the fruit of action is not to be abandoned;
that person who performs the gift with faith and renders service to Kṛṣṇa does so for the sake of abandoning self-interest. (HNC 8.20)
If one causes [others] to perform ritual actions, it results in profit for the priest;
therefore, that is the influence of the Kaitava. (HNC 8.21)
The Vedas and Smṛtis proclaim infinite fruits;
yet those devoid of self-interest do not acknowledge them. (HNC 8.22)
All karma, whether auspicious or inauspicious, rests upon the insentient; the sacrificer offers it and receives its fruit, which is likewise composed of the insentient. (HNC 8.23)
If one casts the fruit of karma far away and performs actions [without attachment], the heart becomes pure; this is the essential point for liberation. (HNC 8.24)
In the pure heart, self-delight is perfectly stainless;
its arising gradually becomes powerful. (HNC 8.25)
The name is composed of consciousness;
since it cannot be a mere figurative description (arthavāda),
that very name is present as self-delight within itself.
At the time of the means of accomplishment, it is prescribed for the object to be accomplished.
The final fruit of action is indeed its name and essence;
this is certain when action is performed in the form of a saintly person. (HNC 8.27)
Therefore, O Brahmin, wander through the fourteen worlds and destroy that which is called "fruit" but does not exist. (HNC 8.28)
The fruit of the Name will certainly be supreme;
for what can a person who performs violence do with the Name, even if they are knowledgeable? (HNC 8.29)
All action remains as the fruit of the knowledge of Brahman within the appearance of name; the fruit of all action is obtained within the appearance of name.
The fruit of all knowledge is attained within the appearance of name. (HNC 8.30)
If these [qualities] meet with a semblance of high fruit, then they are powerful in bestowing even more than that name of a thing. (HNC 8.31)
Therefore, whatever name is praised as a fruit in the scriptures, people who rely on that pure name attain certainty. (HNC 8.32)
There may be doubt regarding the fruit of one's name, but there is no doubt regarding the auspiciousness of that [name]; whoever has such doubt is a base person.
Indeed, upon an offense, a downfall is inevitable. HNC 8.33.
In the Vedas, the Rāmāyaṇa, the Mahābhārata, and the Purāṇas— in the beginning, the end, and the middle— the story of the Lord of the lotus-navel (Hari) is recounted.

Since the scriptural statements regarding the mention of fruits are beginningless and immutable, what purpose would there be in imagining them to be mere *arthavāda* (eulogistic declarations)? (HNC 8.35)

In comparison to the power of karma and knowledge, Your name possesses infinite qualities and power; having bestowed all powers upon the name, You have placed the power of Your name above them all. // HNC_8.36 //
You alone are the independent reality, possessed of all powers; by your will, whatever exists is ordained and established. (HNC 8.37)
The inert matter performs its functions through karma, while Brahman, by its own independent ordinance, bestows the power of liberation through knowledge. (HNC 8.38)
O Lord composed of will, you have bestowed all power upon your own name; what else remains for me to do? (HNC 8.39)
Therefore, you are indeed all-powerful; a wise person should not treat your name as a mere figurative expression (arthavāda). HNC 8.40.
If an offense occurs during the ritual for the expiation of that offense,
one should place a blade of grass between one's teeth in the assembly of Vaiṣṇavas. (HNC 8.41)
Having confessed his offense at the feet of the Vaiṣṇava,
he made a prostration with a sincere mind and begged for forgiveness.
O devotees of the Lord, the greatness of Nāma has been known;
having granted forgiveness and shown mercy, may it bestow its embrace.
Neither names nor discursive explanations, nor conceptualization or reflection—never at any time shall these delusive deceptions arise in the mind. (HNC 8.44)
If one engages in conversation with a person who utters meaningless speech, one should perform an immersion in the waters of the Ganges. (HNC 8.45)
The flute is the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, whose essence is compassion; the name of Hari is the wish-fulfilling jewel, the savior, and the ornament. HNC 8.46.
Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "An Examination of Arthavādas and Offenses," in the *Śrī Hari-nāma-cintāmaṇi*.
(9) Ninth Chapter.
Evil intent arises from the power of name;
for one in whom evil intent does not exist by the power of name, purification indeed comes through the restraints (yamas).
Victory, O fair-complexioned Gadādhara, life of the Ganges!
Victory, victory, O Sītādvaita; victory to the multitude of devotees! HNC_9.1 //
By the power of Hari’s name, which is composed of pure goodness, all misfortunes are removed upon its utterance; therefore, a fortunate soul takes refuge in the Name. (HNC 9.2)
Very swiftly their misfortune departs;
the weakness of heart finds no place to remain. (HNC 9.3)
When the Name becomes firm, there is no inclination toward sin; former sins are burnt away, and the mind becomes exceedingly pure. (HNC 9.4)
Sin, the seed of sin, and the latent impression of sin—ignorance is their root; these three are the machine. (HNC 9.5)
May compassion for all living beings arise; may you constantly perform auspicious deeds for the sake of living beings. (HNC 9.6)
The suffering of a living being can never be endured;
therefore, one should act for the sake of removing the suffering of others. (HNC 9.7)
Thirst for sense objects is utterly trivial in the mind; there is no trace of craving for the senses in their hearts. (HNC 9.8)
One should feel revulsion toward the conduct of a lustful woman for gold as one feels satisfaction upon attaining the Dharma; thus one should sustain one's life.
One should accept everything that is favorable to devotion, and one should not take upon oneself anything that is contrary to devotion. (HNC 9.10)
One should know that Kṛṣṇa alone is the protector;
one should consider Kṛṣṇa here as the sustainer of life. (HNC 9.11)
I do not maintain attachment to the notion of "I" or "mine" in my heart;
at all times, I am absorbed in a state of humility.
If one’s nature is such that it relies upon form and name, what can be done for one whose mind is set on evil and whose conduct is wicked? (HNC 9.13)
Former sins or the scent of sin will quickly be removed; the states previously perceived will gradually diminish, and one’s pure nature will swiftly become proficient. (HNC 9.14)
At the time of this transition, there remains a connection with former sins; for some days, the scent of sin persists. (HNC 9.15)
When the association with Nāma occurs, from which the arising of good intellect follows,
that very scent of sin is quickly destroyed.
O Lord, make this vow in the presence of Arjuna: "My devotee shall never fall into danger. (HNC 9.17)
In times of distress, you alone are my companion;
therefore, through your grace, I shall be freed from sin. (HNC 9.18)
One who follows the path of knowledge, having committed evil through harshness and subjugation, quickly falls away from reliance upon you. HNC_9.19 //
O Great Being, those who take refuge at your feet shall never encounter obstacles; such is the word of the established doctrine.
If sin has arisen due to negligence, there is no purpose in its atonement; yet if some sin should occur through negligence, the devotee does not endure the torment of penance. (HNC 9.21)
That evil is not momentary; it finds no stable state. It is called a "poison" because it leads one to a miserable rebirth. HNC 9.22.
The result for one who commits evil deeds under the power of a name is such; however, if anyone, by means of that name,
should commit new evil, [the consequence will be different].
Such a person is fickle. HNC_9.23 //
Having taken refuge in mere hypocrisy, one incurs the fault of name and the fear of grief and death. (HNC 9.24)
Negligence consists of the distinction between contemplated action and the occurrence of negligence; all its various subdivisions exist within the core of the Bhakti-shastra. (HNC 9.25)
Those who commit sins should remain far from the Name;
for it is an offense against the Name when one sets one's mind upon sin.
Whatever sinful conduct a worldly human being may practice, [it is an offense].
There is expiation for that, and thereafter remorse. (HNC 9.26)
But if one sets one's mind upon sin by the power of one's name, there is no atonement for that; it leads to a very great downfall.
Even if one has experienced many torments of hell and the like, there is no deliverance from that offense. (HNC 9.28)
When even the mere thought of evil is of such a nature as this machine, what need is there to mention the fault of its actual practice? // HNC_9.29 //
The deceptive and crafty one named Bharasā is recorded in the scriptures as having only the "monkey-like dispassion" (*vairāgya*) of a wicked deed; by this, he removes his sins.
Even a great sinner of ten million births cannot accomplish what he has done. (HNC 9.30)
The fivefold sins, including the great transgressions (*mahāpātaka*), have no limit; they are sung in the scriptures by means of their mere names as being without end. (HNC 9.31)
Having become a heavy burden for you, O deceitful person, he takes up the name [of the Buddha] through his craftiness. (HNC 9.32)
Having abandoned worldly existence with great difficulty, he dressed in the garb of a detached ascetic;
yet, driven by the desire for gold and women, he wandered from country to country. (HNC 9.33)
But you, O Lord, are a monkey-like ascetic; having abandoned the house of Dharma, you wander about conversing with women. (HNC 9.34)
If one does not take refuge in the name with sincerity, this offense is unavoidable;
under the guise of renunciation, some pass their time in their homes, for all the worldly entanglements of the universe are not worth conversing about. (HNC 9.35)
There is no fault in staying at home or going to the forest; one finds contentment by receiving the name of Karuṇā from the sinless one. (HNC 9.36)
O Bali, evil-minded one, this great offense will cause an obstacle to your immersion in the reality of devotion. (HNC 9.37)
If one associates with those who bear the name of a hypocrite, then this offense will certainly occur; for such a person becomes an offender by the company of these deceitful people. (HNC 9.38)
In whose heart the pure arising of the Name shall dwell, for that person no offense against this Name shall ever occur. (HNC 9.39)

A person who has taken refuge in the pure Name shall not be touched by the ten kinds of offenses; for one who has taken refuge in the pure Name, no offense whatsoever shall ever touch them in any form or at any time. (HNC 9.40)
For those who rely on the Name, the Name always provides protection; it is impossible for them ever to commit an offense. (HNC 9.41)
On whichever day the pure name does not arise, on that day there is fear from the onset of transgression. (HNC 9.42)
Therefore, if one who merely bears the name of a practitioner appears before you, flee from him; for by the power of that name, the evil-minded one will be destroyed. HNC 9.43.

Should one, day and night, remain vigilant and strive to abandon offenses? By taking recourse to the strength of association with those who have taken shelter of the pure Name, one should always practice the discernment of offenses. (HNC 9.44)
Those in whose mouths the pure name resides have minds so firm that they do not waver from Kṛṣṇa for even a single moment. (HNC 9.45)
Therefore, indeed, pass the days with strength; thus, there will be no fear regarding the transgressions of those days. (HNC 9.46)
Having cast far away thoughts of evil through special effort, one should day and night utter "Hari, Hari" with strength upon the lips. HNC 9.47.
Through the grace of the glorious guru, one attains the knowledge of the true relationship [to Kṛṣṇa];
from that arises devotion to Kṛṣṇa and the chanting of His name. HNC 9.48.
Although one may have committed an offense and,
due to negligence, possess a sinful mind despite the power of the Name, one attains purification by associating with pure Vaiṣṇavas. (HNC 9.49)
The desire for evil was suppressed on the road;
the assembly of pure Vaiṣṇavas protected the path. // HNC_9.50 //
Crying out at the top of their voices, "Dākinīs! Guards! they will flee along the road, while the police will remain behind. (HNC 9.51)
O brother, do not feel fear toward one who is devoted and strong;
O noble-minded one, I am indeed your protector.
For those whose vow is solely the service of the feet of the Vaiṣṇavas, even the wish-fulfilling jewel of Hari’s name becomes like ashes. (HNC 9.53)
Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "The Evil-minded," in the *Śrī Hari-nāma-cintāmaṇi* concerning the power of the Name.

Even toward one who lacks faith, is averse, or does not listen,
whatever instruction is given is an offense against the Name of Śiva:
"Victory to Gaurī’s Gadādhara, the life of the Gaṅgā!"
Victory, victory to Sītā-advaita! Victory to the assembly of devotees!
O Haridāsa, listen to the words of Balena;
hear the name of another offense. // HNC_10.2 //
When there is firm conviction in the Name, faith becomes powerful; by that alone one gains authority over the Name, for in whose heart faith has not arisen, [the Name remains ineffective].
O you who are outward-looking and evil-minded, there is no such thing as a name. // HNC_10.3 //
There is no authority for one who has not been born, nor is there authority for one who is merely born; faith alone is the authority—this is the essence of reality. HNC_10.4 //
Noble birth, noble family,
knowledge,
and power.
There is no reason for granting authority over the wealth of knowledge. // HNC_10.5 //
Whoever possesses firm conviction in the majesty of Nāma and has faith in the teachings of the scriptures, that person shines everywhere. (HNC 10.6)

If one gives the name to a person devoid of faith, it constitutes an offense against the Name; for the Name of Hari does not take birth in one who lacks faith, nor do holy men grant it, nor do they follow the conduct of a Vaiṣṇava [in such a case]. // HNC_10.7 //
If a person devoid of faith should obtain the name of Hari, they will treat it with contempt, even while singing of it in all the scriptures. (HNC 10.8)
If given to a pig, one should grind it into powder with jewels; if given to a monkey, one should scatter torn pieces of clothing. // HNC_10.9 //
One who lacks faith commits what is called the "offense of drinking"; with every step, such a person becomes heavy and quickly becomes unworthy of devotion. HNC_10.10 //

When one encounters a person devoid of faith who has come to offer prayers, how is it appropriate to interact with them? Such a person, lacking faith, acts with deceit and approaches the side of the Vaiṣṇavas to beg for the name of Hari. (HNC 10.11)
The virtuous understand such deceptive speech;
they never give the name of Hari to such a person.
"Excellent, O Balarāma, brother! Abandon deceit;
cast far away the desire for worldly status and place your faith in the Name. (HNC 10.13)
If there is faith in the Name, one attains it without effort;
by the power of the Name, one crosses over this saṃsāra. (HNC 10.14)
Since there is no faith in your name, O brother, you have no right even to utter it. (HNC 10.15)
Having heard the greatness of the holy Name from the mouths of saintly scriptures,
abandon the desire for worldly status and accept it with humility.
If faith exists in the Name, then the Guru and the great people will appear; O brother, one should offer everything to the Name—the Name is the supreme wealth.
The name "Arthalobha" was given to those people who were devoid of faith;
by committing the offense of misappropriating that name, they went to hell. (HNC 10.18)
Although instruction may indeed serve as a remedy for an offense when it arises from negligence,
for one devoid of faith, encountering a guru brings great fear. (HNC 10.19)
Having made such a representation in the Vaiṣṇava assembly, the great personage shall abandon that wicked disciple. (HNC 10.20)
If one does not act accordingly, it results in a succession of offenses against the Guru;
devoid of devotion and following evil conduct, one remains in the delusion of Māyā. (HNC 10.21)
Therefore, whenever the Lord issues a command and the name is proclaimed, he gives this instruction: HNC_10.22.
In this matter, what need is there for instruction to those who have faith in the Lord’s command? May the majesty of His name fill every land. // HNC_10.23 //
One should cultivate faith in the proclamation of the Name and spread it abroad; the living being who attains such faith will engage in reflection upon the True Guru. HNC 10.24.
One should take up the chanting of the holy Name in the presence of a true guru;
then, without effort, one attains the wealth of love for Kṛṣṇa.
Having caused those people who are attached to sin—such as thieves, prostitutes, and rogues—to abandon their sinful thoughts, one should bestow faith upon them through wealth. (HNC 10.26)
If there is great faith, the instruction of the Name will be given;
in this manner, the Name is bestowed upon him throughout his entire life.
This form is not the fruit of one's offenses; it is not even called wealth here. Yet, because of those very offenses, one falls into hell. (HNC 10.28)
If a disciple commits even a slight offense, it becomes an obstacle to the savor of devotion for the guru. (HNC 10.29)
If a disciple commits this offense against the guru, he shall go to hell; this offense is indeed grave. (HNC 10.30)
"O Madhava, you have shown great compassion toward the world by bestowing faith in the Name;
O Gaura Hari, having given the Name, you have bestowed faith in the Name. (HNC 10.31)
O you whose conduct is marvelous, may all the hosts of people, having developed faith, follow your compassionate footsteps.
The devotee who takes pleasure in devotion to the feet [of the Lord] wears the ornament of the *hari-nāma-cintāmaṇi*. // HNC_10.33 // (11) Chapter Eleven.

Even the equality of all auspicious activities— such as knowledge equal to that of the Name, religious vows, renunciation, and fire-offerings— is negligence when accompanied by other auspicious actions.
Victory, victory to Gauracandra, the incarnation whose very name is the essence of all reality; victory, victory to the Name of Hari, the quintessence of all truths! HNC_11.1 //
O Kṛṣṇa, the name is the means and the sentient being is the goal; the Lord is the reality of perfect bliss.
Whether it be the goal, the attainment, the offering, or the consumption, its greatness is supreme. (HNC 11.26)
The means has appeared on the surface of the earth through these two;
the identity of the goal and the means is the strength of all scriptures. (HNC 11.27)
In the distinction of the [spiritual] capacities, there are three means (upāya) which are the essential nature; the others are the three goals (upeya), which are of a different form. HNC 11.28.
Auspicious action is the secondary means (gauṇopāya), while the primary means (mukhyopāya) is the abode of qualities; thus, the means are twofold:
auspicious action is the secondary means, and [the Lord] is called the primary means. // HNC_11.29 //
The name is beyond the reach of the senses;
therefore, in the scripture, whatever other auspicious karma exists does not coexist with the name—this is the essential secret of all the scriptures. (HNC 11.30)
When one sings the name of Kṛṣṇa with a simple heart,
a bliss beyond the senses arises within the mind without effort.
Be happy, intent on the nature of Kṛṣṇa’s name;
find delight in the Self and sport with the Self—there is no one else for you. (HNC 11.32)

The bliss of union (*sāyujya*) and absolute liberation (*kaivalya*), the splendor of bliss in the yoga of Brahman-knowledge, is but a mere shadow of true happiness; it is merely the experience of the shadow of bliss that arises from the cessation of insentience. (HNC 11.33)
Consider the bliss of indivisible liberation as a very small offering; consider the overflowing bliss of the joy in Kṛṣṇa’s name as the true offering. HNC 11.34.
Other than through virtuous deeds, the name is the means at the time of practice due to its distinct nature; at the time of attainment, it is the goal, which is of a different character. (HNC 11.35)
The very nature of the means is established as being the state of the goal; it is well known that such is not the case with other virtuous actions.
All other auspicious karmas depend upon the insentient; but that which is called Consciousness is eternally self-established and manifest.
The time for practice is called pure and utterly stainless; it appears as stained to the practitioner due to his own misfortune. (HNC 11.38)
By taking the name "Sādhusaṅga," one becomes dull-witted;
yet, when all misfortunes have been completely eliminated, the name becomes pure. (HNC 11.39)
Abandoning other auspicious actions as a means, one should take recourse in the ultimate state, the final support. (HNC 11.40)
However, a person who relies on the name does not abandon the name;
he resorts to the mere purity of the name at the time of attaining accomplishment. (HNC 11.41)
Distinct from all other auspicious karmas, the true nature of Nāma possesses an unprecedented characteristic. (HNC 11.42)
This extraordinary knowledge belongs to the stage of spiritual practice;
it arises through the grace of the Guru and is validated by the authority of the Vedas. (HNC 11.43)
Those who are devoid of this knowledge regarding the stage of accomplishment are offenders by name; they are extremely modern. (HNC 11.44)
There is no name superior to this name; bring nothing equal to it. Having firm conviction in this, one should dissolve into this very name. (HNC 11.45)
O Lord whose pure name brings about awakening, may you swiftly quench my thirst; O Pūrṇānanda, make me take refuge in the essence of Your name. HNC 11.46.
Even if one performs other auspicious deeds as a remedy for this offense,
the mind remains bound by evil actions as if tethered by a name. (HNC 11.47)
One should make an effort for the exhaustion of misdeeds;
through the Name, one attains pure intellect and the wealth of love. (HNC 11.48)
O householder, you who are devoted to the pure name of the *antyaja*, I shall rub the dust of your feet upon my body as an ointment. (HNC 11.49)
One shall eat the nectar of the lips and drink the water from the feet;
then the mind, purified by the Name, will become stainless. (HNC 11.50)
O Kālīdāsa, in this manner, sing for the people of the world how you destroyed your wicked deeds and again obtained Your mercy. HNC 11.51.
O Lord, we of dull intellect have sung only this much:
we have never found the true nature of the wish-fulfilling jewel that is Your name. (HNC 11.52)
O Lord, having bestowed Your grace upon my tongue regarding the name of Haridāsa Ṭhākura, please hold the feet of Your servant and dance incessantly with the Name. (HNC 11.53)
Keep this [name] here; let that be according to your will. Grant me the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s name as my very body.
O Diti, you have indeed descended among the people of the world;
in the midst of the world’s folk, may my hand be accepted [as yours].
I am the lowest, you are the lowest, yet you are my savior; this connection between us two is the purifier of the fallen.
This indestructible bond belongs to you and me;
by its power, even this lowest of men has become immortal.
In the Kali age, by what means can the duties of the [preceding] ages be accomplished?
Other auspicious actions are very difficult to achieve in the Kali age; therefore, the name [of this age] was established as "the age of names" (nāma-yuga). HNC 11.58.
O people, this servant of the servants of Haridāsa, Bhaktivinoda,
a man of nothing, sings the *Hari-nāma-cintāmaṇi*. (HNC 11.59) (12) Chapter Twelve.

Having performed the chanting of the Name through the grace of Jāṅgidera, // HNC_12.1 //
The offense known as negligence was committed by Haridāsa against the eternal Lord;
furthermore, Gopālabhaṭṭa [committed it] during his pilgrimage to the south. // HNC_12.2 //
One should count heedfulness as the crest-lock and the worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa as the head, while counting negligence as an offense. (HNC 12.3)
Even if one abandons all other offenses and is always absorbed in the Name, if there is no love for the Name, it will not arise. (HNC 12.4)
Then, knowing this, one realizes that the offense called negligence creates an obstacle to the practice of love and devotion. (HNC 12.5)
Inattentiveness is the power of negligence;
this is the essential meaning of "negligence" and "inattentiveness. From this, O Lord, all manner of misfortunes arise. (HNC 12.6)
There are three kinds of inattention: indifference, dullness, and distraction;
one who is skilled should understand these three types of inattention.
Until one becomes filled with devotion, it is necessary to make an effort in chanting the Name;
if by some fortune any living being possesses faith, then let them chant the Name of Hari. (HNC 12.8)
If one makes an effort to remember the name along with its numerical count,
then love for the name arises and becomes manifest.
Those for whom the arising of attachment has reached its limit, they always dissolve into the Name by exerting effort to that very limit. HNC 12.10.
In the absence of effort, the practitioner's mind is not stable by nature;
all people are attached to sense objects, and at the time of mindfulness, they remain enamored with other objects. (HNC 12.11)
One may be indifferent toward other matters according to one's inclination, but one should never be distracted in mind during the daily recitation. HNC 12.12.
The mind is directed toward one thing and named after another; how can there be auspiciousness for such a one who is a mere abode of qualities? (HNC 12.13)
If one counts a full rosary by the name of "lakṣa," there is no drop of nectar in the heart, nor any jewel of virtue. (HNC 12.14)
Indeed, this is a variety of the fault of negligence;
for one whose heart is attached to sense objects, the Lord is very difficult to restrain. (HNC 12.15)
The method for making an effort is to abandon sense objects for even a short time in the company of holy beings; by staying in a secluded place, these faults are destroyed. HNC 12.16.
Step by step, the mind becomes steady through the name of Kṛṣṇa;
it becomes restless in the continuous savoring of that name.
Dwell in the vicinity of the Tulasī plant, in places where the pastimes of Kṛṣṇa take place, in the presence of holy men, and according to the Satvata injunctions.
Gradually increasing the duration of time, one should remember that name;
thus, one will very swiftly cross over the desire for sense objects.
Another method:
by adopting this form, there will be no negligence in the form of indifference;
or else, dwell in a secluded place and remember the conduct of the saintly.
Having restrained the senses, one should apply the mind to the Name.
In the swift [path], there is the culmination of interest in the stages;
in the horse-like [path], there is the destruction of the fault of indifference in the stages of crossing. HNC 12.21.
In those whose minds are dull due to the lack of attentiveness born of stupidity,
there is no interest in the chanting of the holy name. (HNC 12.22)
Furthermore, at the time of recollection, if there is a rapid cessation [of the flow], effort is required; indeed, due to this defect, the flavor of the Name is not revealed. (HNC 12.23)
In other matters, time should not be spent in vain;
the assembly of holy men, reflecting on this, should remember [the Lord] at every moment.
One should remember the Name, immerse oneself in its flavor, and desire nothing else; such a person is a true saint, for these faults do not occur in his company.
One should seek out such a form [of conduct] and associate with the company of the virtuous;
by emulating them, one should abandon the dullness of the mind.
Seeing that he has practiced the Dharma with time spent not in vain, it is certain that one will develop a taste for it. (HNC 12.27)
O mind, when will you find one equal to him? Only a fortunate person would remember or utter his name. (HNC 12.28)
That same enthusiasm which resides in the mind of the indolent, when applied to the remembrance of Kṛṣṇa’s name, removes all dullness. (HNC 12.29)
Today I shall recite one hundred thousand names;
in due course, I shall remember three hundred thousand names.
O Great Seizer, do not hold such a thought; by counting [the breaths], dullness will soon depart through the compassion of the Holy One. HNC_12.31 //
When distraction— which is characterized by a lack of attention produced by mental agitation—
is eliminated, whatever negligence arises is destroyed through great effort. (HNC 12.32)
The desire for gold, women, victory, and defeat, as well as the hope for status and deceitful conduct—these are the abode of that [mind]. (HNC 12.33)
All these manifestations arise within the heart; their non-attention is by nature like a horse. (HNC 12.34)
By gradually abandoning distractions through the successive stages of means, he who has relinquished all such anxieties is indeed a fortunate Vaiṣṇava ascetic in his conduct. (HNC 12.35)
From this very first day, abandon all thought of worldly enjoyment;
in the company of the virtuous, chant the name of Hari day and night. HNC_12.36 //
In the field of Hari, in the service of Hari, in the scripture of Hari, in absorption, in festival, in immersion, and in bliss that is supremely fearless. (HNC 12.37)
In due course, one should increase the time spent in devotion;
one should immerse the mind in the great festival of Hari’s stories.
The supreme flavor will arise in the mind through this sequence;
one will certainly abandon the base flavors of the insentient. (HNC 12.39)
O mind, be enchanted by hearing the songs of Hari from the mouths of great souls; O ear, relish the taste of that nectar. (HNC 12.40)
Desire for inferior objects has vanished;
the mind remains steadfast and unwavering in the singing of the Name. (HNC 12.41)
Therefore, with great effort, one should abandon negligence; one should immerse oneself for many days in the nectar called a steady mind. (HNC 12.42)
In order to complete the number of names conceived through resolute intention,
one should look again and again at the name "Ayatna" (Effortless). HNC 12.43.
Performing the chanting of the Name with vigilance, abandon negligence and practice the worship of the Name.
With a one-pointed mind, having made an insatiable longing for your name continuous through the power of your grace. // HNC_12.45 //
O Lord, please show mercy; let there be no negligence regarding Your name.
Let the savoring of the taste of Your name not fail within my heart.
O devotee, for even a very brief moment in a secluded place with a one-pointed mind, you should practice the recollection of the Name. (HNC 12.47)
Therefore, I clearly consider this state of being [the goal] as the ascendant;
may this prayer always be at Your feet. // HNC_12.48 //
Even if one exerts oneself, no one in this cycle of worldly existence can cross over it without your grace. (HNC 12.49)
The necessity of grasping with effort:
this is certainly required when calling out a name without guile; it is not, however, an offense.
Having made an effort and entreated you with an agitated heart,
O Compassionate One, please bestow your grace upon me hereafter.
If you do not make an effort to obtain your grace,
then I am indeed devoid of fortune, O son of Śacī.

O Lord, this is the most base offense;
because of this fault, love for Your name does not arise. (HNC 13.3)
